   394→// ============================================================================
   395→// Forward Pass
   396→// ============================================================================
   397→
   398→float* forward(Transformer* transformer, int token, int pos) {
   399→    Config* p = &transformer->config;
   400→    TransformerWeights* w = &transformer->weights;
   401→    RunState* s = &transformer->state;
   402→
   403→    int dim = p->dim;
   404→    int kv_dim = (dim * p->n_kv_heads) / p->n_heads;
   405→    int kv_mul = p->n_heads / p->n_kv_heads;
   406→    int hidden_dim = p->hidden_dim;
   407→    int head_size = dim / p->n_heads;
   408→
   409→    if (token < 0 || token >= p->vocab_size) {
   410→        return nullptr;
   411→    }
   412→
   413→    // Copy token embedding
   414→    float* content_row = w->token_embedding_table + token * dim;
   415→    memcpy(s->x, content_row, dim * sizeof(float));
   416→
   417→    // Forward through all layers
   418→    for (int l = 0; l < p->n_layers; l++) {
   419→        rmsnorm(s->xb, s->x, w->rms_att_weight + l * dim, dim);
   420→
   421→        int loff = l * p->seq_len * kv_dim;
   422→        s->k = s->key_cache + loff + pos * kv_dim;
   423→        s->v = s->value_cache + loff + pos * kv_dim;
   424→
   425→        quantize(&s->xq, s->xb, dim);
   426→        matmul_q8(s->q, &s->xq, &w->wq[l], dim, dim);
   427→        matmul_q8(s->k, &s->xq, &w->wk[l], dim, kv_dim);
   428→        matmul_q8(s->v, &s->xq, &w->wv[l], dim, kv_dim);
   429→
   430→        // RoPE with cached sin/cos lookup (eliminates runtime trig)
   431→        int half_head = head_size / 2;
   432→        float* cos_ptr = transformer->rope_cos + pos * half_head;
   433→        float* sin_ptr = transformer->rope_sin + pos * half_head;
   434→
   435→        for (int i = 0; i < dim; i += 2) {
   436→            int idx = (i / 2) % half_head;
   437→            float fcr = cos_ptr[idx];
   438→            float fci = sin_ptr[idx];
   439→            int rotn = i < kv_dim ? 2 : 1;
   440→            for (int v = 0; v < rotn; v++) {
   441→                float* vec = v == 0 ? s->q : s->k;
   442→                float v0 = vec[i];
   443→                float v1 = vec[i + 1];
   444→                vec[i] = v0 * fcr - v1 * fci;
   445→                vec[i + 1] = v0 * fci + v1 * fcr;
   446→            }
   447→        }
   448→
   449→        // Multi-head attention with SIMD
   450→        float scale = 1.0f / sqrtf(head_size);
   451→        for (int h = 0; h < p->n_heads; h++) {
   452→            float* q = s->q + h * head_size;
   453→            float* att = s->att + h * p->seq_len;
   454→
   455→            // Attention scoring with SIMD dot product
   456→            for (int t = 0; t <= pos; t++) {
   457→                float* k = s->key_cache + loff + t * kv_dim + (h / kv_mul) * head_size;
   458→                float score = 0.0f;
   459→                dsps_dotprod_f32_aes3(q, k, &score, head_size);
   460→                att[t] = score * scale;
   461→            }
   462→
   463→            softmax(att, pos + 1);
   464→
   465→            // Attention aggregation with SIMD
   466→            float* xb = s->xb + h * head_size;
   467→            memset(xb, 0, head_size * sizeof(float));
   468→            for (int t = 0; t <= pos; t++) {
   469→                float* v = s->value_cache + loff + t * kv_dim + (h / kv_mul) * head_size;
   470→                float a = att[t];
   471→                // xb += a * v using SIMD: temp = v * a, xb += temp
   472→                dsps_mulc_f32_ae32(v, s->xb2, head_size, a, 1, 1);
   473→                dsps_add_f32_ae32(xb, s->xb2, xb, head_size, 1, 1, 1);
   474→            }
   475→        }
   476→
   477→        quantize(&s->xq, s->xb, dim);
   478→        matmul_q8(s->xb2, &s->xq, &w->wo[l], dim, dim);
   479→
   480→        // Residual connection with SIMD
   481→        dsps_add_f32_ae32(s->x, s->xb2, s->x, dim, 1, 1, 1);
   482→
   483→        rmsnorm(s->xb, s->x, w->rms_ffn_weight + l * dim, dim);
   484→
   485→        quantize(&s->xq, s->xb, dim);
   486→        matmul_q8(s->hb, &s->xq, &w->w1[l], dim, hidden_dim);
   487→        matmul_q8(s->hb2, &s->xq, &w->w3[l], dim, hidden_dim);
   488→
   489→        // SwiGLU with fast sigmoid approximation
   490→        // sigmoid(x) ≈ 0.5 + 0.5 * tanh(x * 0.5) ≈ x / (1 + |x|) for speed
   491→        // But for SiLU we need decent accuracy, use: 1/(1+exp(-x)) ≈ fast approx
   492→        for (int i = 0; i < hidden_dim; i += 4) {
   493→            // Unrolled for better pipelining
   494→            float v0 = s->hb[i], v1 = s->hb[i+1], v2 = s->hb[i+2], v3 = s->hb[i+3];
   495→            // SiLU: x * sigmoid(x)
   496→            v0 *= 1.0f / (1.0f + expf(-v0));
   497→            v1 *= 1.0f / (1.0f + expf(-v1));
   498→            v2 *= 1.0f / (1.0f + expf(-v2));
   499→            v3 *= 1.0f / (1.0f + expf(-v3));
   500→            // Gate multiply
   501→            s->hb[i]   = v0 * s->hb2[i];
   502→            s->hb[i+1] = v1 * s->hb2[i+1];
   503→            s->hb[i+2] = v2 * s->hb2[i+2];
   504→            s->hb[i+3] = v3 * s->hb2[i+3];
   505→        }
   506→
   507→        quantize(&s->hq, s->hb, hidden_dim);
   508→        matmul_q8(s->xb, &s->hq, &w->w2[l], hidden_dim, dim);
   509→
   510→        // Residual connection with SIMD
   511→        dsps_add_f32_ae32(s->x, s->xb, s->x, dim, 1, 1, 1);
   512→    }
   513→
   514→    rmsnorm(s->x, s->x, w->rms_final_weight, dim);
   515→
   516→    quantize(&s->xq, s->x, dim);
   517→    matmul_q8(s->logits, &s->xq, w->wcls, dim, p->vocab_size);
   518→
   519→    return s->logits;
   520→}
   521→

## TRAINING PIPELINES SUMMARY

### 1. AUDIO SEMANTIC EMBEDDING PIPELINE (XTTS-v2)
**Location:** `/home/alphons/project/OAISYS25/badge/workbench/tests/audio_semantic_xtts_ipynb/`

#### Pipeline Overview
Trains an audio-text semantic embedding model using XTTS-v2 (Coqui TTS) for voice synthesis and YAMNet for audio feature extraction.

**Key Components:**
- **Audio Generation:** Coqui XTTS-v2 (human-like speech synthesis with speaker cloning)
- **Audio Features:** YAMNet (1024-dim embeddings)
- **Text Features:** SentenceTransformers MiniLM-L6-v2 (384-dim embeddings)
- **Projection:** Learnable 256-dim shared embedding space with batch normalization

#### Datasets & Inputs
| Aspect | Details |
|--------|---------|
| **Base Queries** | 10 intent queries (schedule, booth, navigation, contact, notes, map, messages, profile, session, connect) |
| **Text Variations** | 10 variations per query = 100 unique texts total |
| **Speakers** | 8 diverse TED speakers (male/female, various accents): BillGates, DaphneKoller, FeiFeiLi, JaneGoodall, SalmanKhan, GeorgeTakei, StephenHawking, StephenWolfram |
| **Audio Samples** | 400 total (100 texts × 2 speakers per text × 2x augmentation) |
| **Augmentation** | Gaussian noise, time stretch, pitch shift |

#### Model Architecture
```
Audio Projection (2.53 MB):
  Input: YAMNet embeddings (1024-dim)
  → BatchNorm + Dense(512) + ReLU
  → BatchNorm + Dropout(0.2)
  → Dense(256) + L2 Normalization
  → Output: 256-dim normalized embedding

Text Projection (391 KB):
  Input: MiniLM embeddings (384-dim)
  → BatchNorm
  → Dense(256) + L2 Normalization
  → Output: 256-dim normalized embedding

Total: 662K parameters (2.91 MB combined)
```

#### Training Process
- **Epochs:** 500 (increased from 300 for better convergence)
- **Loss:** Contrastive loss (temperature=0.2)
- **Learning Rate:** 3e-4 with ReduceLROnPlateau (factor=0.5, patience=20)
- **Batch Size:** 16
- **Dataset Split:** No explicit val set; uses training accuracy

#### Performance Metrics
| Metric | Result |
|--------|--------|
| **Pair Matching Accuracy** | 24.5% (correctly matches audio to text variation) |
| **Base Query Accuracy** | 100% (matches to correct base intent class) |
| **Correct Pair Similarity** | 0.844 (diagonal values) |
| **Incorrect Pair Similarity** | -0.002 (off-diagonal values) |
| **Similarity Gap** | 0.846 (excellent separation) |

#### Output Files for ESP32
```
models_xtts/
├── audio_projection.h5                    # Full model (2.53 MB)
├── audio_projection_quantized.tflite      # Quantized (663 KB) - USE THIS
├── query_embeddings.bin                   # Pre-computed embeddings (10 KB)
│                                          # 10 queries × 256-dim × 4 bytes
└── query_texts.txt                        # Query reference labels
```

**ESP32 Deployment Size:** ~3.5 MB total
- YAMNet model: ~2.8 MB
- Projection head: ~663 KB
- Query embeddings: ~10 KB

#### Fine-Tuning Strategy (from FINE_TUNING_GUIDE.md)
**Current performance:** 24.5% pair, 100% base query
**Target:** 80-95% with fine-tuning

**Best Approach:** Add real voice recordings
- Record 50-200 diverse speakers (5-10 people)
- 1-2 variations per query per person
- 2-4 hours effort → +60-70% accuracy improvement
- Use lower learning rate (1e-4) to avoid catastrophic forgetting
- Mix real + XTTS data 50:50

**Implementation:** See `finetune_example.py` and FINE_TUNING_GUIDE.md for full pipeline

### 2. LLM Q&A TRAINING PIPELINE (llama2.c Port)
**Location:** `/home/alphons/project/OAISYS25/badge/workbench/tests/llm_qa_scaled_training/`

#### Pipeline Overview
Three-phase training of personalized Q&A LLMs based on llama2.c with custom profile and Q&A data.

**Key Architecture:**
- **Base:** llama2.c (Andrej Karpathy's minimal Llama-2 implementation)
- **Tokenizer:** SentencePiece BPE (configurable vocab size)
- **Framework:** PyTorch with mixed precision training
- **Quantization:** INT8 Q8_0 format for ESP32

#### Configuration (From Notebook)
```
MODEL_SIZES: 1M, 2M, 3M, 4M, 5M, 6M parameters
VOCAB_SIZES: 512, 768, 1024 tokens
CURRENT CONFIG (in notebook): 6M model, 1024 vocab

Model Architecture (6M example):
  - Embedding dim: 224
  - Hidden dim: 896
  - Layers: 8
  - Attention heads: 8
  - KV heads: 4 (grouped query attention)
  - Max sequence: 256 tokens
  - Dropout: 0.1

Training batch: 128
Device: CUDA (Tesla V100)
```

#### Datasets & Inputs

| Phase | Purpose | Data Source | Size | Steps | LR |
|-------|---------|-------------|------|-------|-----|
| **P1 Stories** | Language foundation | TinyStories (100K stories sampled) | 172 MB | 20,000 | 3e-4 |
| **P2 Profile** | Domain grounding (NO stories) | GPT-extracted prose (51 paragraphs × 100) + synthetic Q&A (242 pairs) | 1.45 MB | 10,000 | 1e-4 |
| **P3 Q&A** | Instruction tuning / memorization | Real Q&A dataset (2,008 pairs × 50x repetition) | 7.80 MB | 12,000 | 5e-5 |

#### Data Generation (GPT-Powered)
**Profile Extraction Pipeline:**
1. **Prose Generation:** GPT-4 extracts 50+ diverse prose paragraphs from profile
   - Multiple angles on same facts (professional, casual, narrative styles)
   - Covers: identity, skills, work history, education, projects, interests
   
2. **Fact Extraction:** GPT-4 extracts structured JSON with all profile details
   - Personal info, work history, education, skills, projects, certifications
   
3. **Synthetic Q&A:** GPT-4 generates 300+ Q&A pairs by category
   - Identity & Contact (50 pairs)
   - Current Work (50 pairs)
   - Skills & Expertise (50 pairs)
   - Work History (40 pairs)
   - Education & Certs (30 pairs)
   - Projects & Achievements (40 pairs)
   - Personal & Interests (40 pairs)
   
   **Critical:** All Q&A removes commas/periods from answers to avoid CSV parsing issues

#### Training Process

RESUME CAPABILITY: Saves state_file.json after each checkpoint
  - Allows resuming interrupted training

CHECKPOINTS:
  - Every 1,000 steps (best.pt + step_N.pt)
  - Automatic early stopping: patience=1,000 steps

LOSS TRACKING:
  - Real-time CSV logging (phase, step, train_loss, val_loss, lr)
  - Plot generation every 100 steps
  - Gradient clipping: 1.0
```

### 3. ESP32 INTEGRATION OVERVIEW

#### How Models Connect to Firmware

**Audio Semantic Pipeline (on-device inference):**
```cpp
// ESP32 sketch flow:
1. Record user speech → 3 sec audio @ 16kHz
2. Run YAMNet on audio → 1024-dim embedding
3. Run projection head (TFLite) → 256-dim embedding
4. Cosine similarity vs 10 pre-computed query embeddings
5. Return highest-match query intent
```

**LLM Q&A Pipeline (on-device inference):**
```cpp
// ESP32 sketch flow:
1. Receive user text (from voice transcription or keyboard)
2. Tokenize with SentencePiece tokenizer
3. Run llama2.c quantized model → token-by-token generation
4. Detokenize response using SentencePiece
5. Return answer to user
```

#### Model Files Needed for SD Card
```
SD:/models/
├── audio_semantic/
│   ├── audio_projection_q80.tflite      # Projection head (663 KB)
│   ├── query_embeddings.bin             # Pre-computed embeddings (10 KB)
│   └── query_texts.txt                  # Query labels
│
└── llm_qa/
    ├── ajv009_6M_1024TK_q80.bin         # LLM weights (5.98 MB)
    └── ajv009_1024TK.bin                # Tokenizer (12.9 KB)

Total: ~6.6 MB (fits easily on SD card)
```

#### Update Mechanism
1. **Colab Training:** Generate new models using notebooks
2. **Download:** INT8 quantized (.tflite for audio, .bin for LLM)
3. **SD Card:** Copy to `/models/` directory
4. **ESP32:** Sketch reads from SD card on boot
5. **No firmware recompile needed** - just swap model files

## Technical Summary: OAISYS25 Badge Firmware Prototypes

I've thoroughly examined the three working prototypes. Here's a detailed technical analysis:

## 1. 00_video_loop_btn_pause_gyro_rotate

**File**: `/home/alphons/project/OAISYS25/badge/workbench/working_protos/00_video_loop_btn_pause_gyro_rotate/00_video_loop_btn_pause_gyro_rotate.ino` + `MjpegClass.h`

### Hardware Initialization
- **Display (LCD)**: ST7789 via Arduino_GFX_Library
  - SPI bus: MOSI=38, MISO=40, SCK=39
  - Control: CS=45, DC=42, BL=1
  - Resolution: 240×320 pixels (IPS mode)
- **IMU (QMI8658)**: I2C address 0x6B
  - I2C: SDA=48, SCL=47
  - Reads accelerometer Y-axis for orientation detection
- **Button (BOOT)**: GPIO 0
  - OneButton library for debouncing
- **Backlight**: GPIO 1 (digital output)

### Core Architectures

**MemoryStream Class**:
- Minimal Stream implementation for PSRAM buffer access
- Provides `available()`, `read()`, `peek()`, `readBytes()` interface
- Maintains position pointer for sequential playback
- Implements `reset()` for looping

**VideoPlayer Class** (Singleton pattern):
- Encapsulates display, MJPEG decoder, and state management
- Three state flags: `paused`, `powered`
- JPEG callback static method for JPEGDEC integration
- `begin()` loads entire MJPEG from flash to PSRAM
- `play()` decodes frame-by-frame with loop reset

**OrientationManager Class** (State machine):
```
State Machine Design:
- currentRotation: Stable state (1=USB right, 3=USB left)
- pendingRotation: Candidate during debounce
- Hysteresis: ±0.5g threshold on accelY
- Debounce time: 1000ms stability required
- Poll rate: 20Hz (50ms intervals)

Transitions:
1. Desired = Current: Cancel pending → no change
2. Pending = 0: Start new transition with timestamp
3. Pending = Desired: Check if debounce elapsed → commit or continue
4. Pending ≠ Desired: Restart debounce (flicker rejection)

Output: One-shot `hasChanged()` flag triggers display rotation
```

**MjpegClass**:
- Searches for JPEG markers (0xFFD8 start, 0xFFD9 end)
- Reads in 1024-byte chunks with sliding window
- Extracts complete JPEG frames from MJPEG stream
- Uses JPEGDEC library for hardware-accelerated decoding
- Auto-scales JPEG to fit screen (handles 1/1, 1/2, 1/4, 1/8)
- JPEG draw callback writes directly to framebuffer

### Memory Management
- **PSRAM allocation**: Entire MJPEG video file
  - `ps_malloc(file_size)` for videoBuf
  - `malloc(320*240/2)` for JPEGDEC decode buffer (heap)
- **No dynamic allocation during playback** - all fixed size

### Main Loop
```
loop():
  orientationMgr.update()        // Poll IMU every 50ms
  if orientation_changed:
    player.setRotation()          // Update display
  button.tick()                   // OneButton debounce
  player.play()                   // Decode one frame
```

**Framerate**: Dependent on MJPEG file and JPEG decode speed (not fixed)

### Button Patterns
- **Single click**: `togglePause()` - pause/resume playback
- **Long press**: `togglePower()` - blank screen + backlight off

### Failure Handling
- IMU init failure: Sets `imuAvailable=false`, continues without rotation
- Video load failure: LED blink at 2Hz until reset

**File**: `/home/alphons/project/OAISYS25/badge/workbench/working_protos/02_speaker_mic_combo/02_speaker_mic_combo.ino`

### Hardware Setup

**Microphones (I2S0 - RX)**:
- 2× INMP441 MEMS microphones
- Shared I2S bus: BCK=GPIO2, WS=GPIO4, DIN=GPIO18
- Channel selection via L/R pin:
  - Mic #1 (LEFT): L/R → GND

- I2S config: 32-bit samples, stereo, 16kHz
- DMA: 4 buffers × 1024 samples

**Speaker (I2S1 - TX)**:
- MAX98357A Class-D amplifier
- I2S pins: BCLK=GPIO6, LRC=GPIO7, DIN=GPIO8
- I2S config: 16-bit mono, 16kHz
- Power: 5V preferred (9dB gain), 3.3V works
- Volume controlled via GAIN pin

**LED Feedback**: GPIO 1
- Blinking (200ms period): Recording
- Solid: Playback

### Audio Pipeline

**1. Recording Phase**:
```
I2S0 DMA → i2s_buffer[512] (int32_t)
  ↓ (every loop iteration)
Extract upper 16 bits → stereo_buffer (PSRAM)
  
Duration: 30 seconds
Stereo samples: 960,000 (2 × 16k × 30)
Stereo memory: 1.92 MB PSRAM
```

**2. Downmix Phase** (HYBRID algorithm):
```cpp
For each mono sample i:
  left = stereo_buffer[i*2]
  right = stereo_buffer[i*2+1]
  
  // Exponential moving average (EMA) of energy
  left_energy = left_energy * 0.95 + |left| * 0.05
  right_energy = right_energy * 0.95 + |right| * 0.05
  
  // Calculate weights
  total = left_energy + right_energy
  left_weight = left_energy / total
  
  // Constrain: 30% ≤ weight ≤ 70%
  left_weight = clamp(left_weight, 0.3, 0.7)
  right_weight = 1.0 - left_weight
  
  // Mix with 4x gain boost (hardware gain compensation)
  mixed = (left * left_weight + right * right_weight) * 4.0
  mono_buffer[i] = clamp(mixed, -32768, 32767)
```

**Key insight**: Adaptive weighting prevents "interruption" when blocking one mic while maintaining stereo width (30%-70% constraint ensures both channels always contribute).

**3. Normalization**:
- Find peak level in recording
- Calculate: `norm_gain = 32000.0 / peak` (max 8x boost)
- Apply sample-by-sample with clipping protection

**4. Playback**:
```
mono_buffer → I2S1 DMA (2048-sample chunks) → Speaker loop forever
```

### Buffer Management
- Recording: 1.92 MB stereo PSRAM
- After downmix: 960 KB mono PSRAM
- Output buffer: 2048 samples stack

### Error Handling
- PSRAM allocation failure: `error_blink()` (200ms LED toggle)
- I2S init failure: Same error blink
- Recording I2S read failure: Return false, trigger error blink

## 3. 03_custom_wakeword

**File**: `/home/alphons/project/OAISYS25/badge/workbench/working_protos/03_custom_wakeword/03_custom_wakeword.ino`

### Hardware Setup

**Microphone (I2S0 - RX)**:
- Single INMP441 (mono input)
- I2S: BCK=GPIO2, WS=GPIO4, DIN=GPIO18
- I2S config: 32-bit samples, left channel only, 16kHz
- DMA: 4 buffers × 256 samples

**SD Card**:
- SPI pins: SCK=39, MOSI=38, MISO=40, CS=41
- Load paths:
  - Config: `/models/hey_daisy.json`
  - Model: `/models/hey_daisy.tflite`

**LED**: GPIO 1 (detection feedback)

### TensorFlow Lite Integration

**Tensor Arena Allocation**:
```cpp
tensor_arena = ps_malloc(500 KB)       // Model weights + activation
var_arena = ps_malloc(50 KB)           // Variable state for streaming
resource_vars = MicroResourceVariables // For recurrent layers
```

**Model Loading**:
- Load from SD card to PSRAM at startup
- Check TFLITE_SCHEMA_VERSION compatibility
- Input: Quantized int8 or float, shape [1, 3, 40] (3 frames × 40-bin spectrogram)
- Output: Single probability (uint8, int8, or float)

**Quantization Support**:
- Input: Supports int8 and float
  - Int8: `scaled = (feature_buffer[i] * 256 + 333) / 666 - 128`
  - Float: `scaled = feature_buffer[i] / 25.6`
- Output: Supports uint8, int8, float
  - Dequantize: `probability = (raw - zero_point) * scale`

### Audio Feature Pipeline

**Microfrontend** (TensorFlow audio preprocessing):
```
I2S0 audio (16kHz, 16-bit) 
  ↓
FrontendProcessSamples()
  - 30ms Hamming window
  - 10ms stride (overlap)
  - FFT (ESP-DSP accelerated)
  - Log-mel filterbank (40 bins)
  - Noise reduction (even/odd smoothing)
  - PCAN gain control (adaptive normalization)
  ↓
Output: 40-bin spectrogram frame (uint16_t)
```

**Feature Buffer Management**:
```
audio_buffer[1024]           // Rolling audio ringbuffer
  ↓
FrontendProcessSamples() called when audio_buffer_pos ≥ 160 samples (10ms)
  ↓
feature_buffer[120]          // 3 frames × 40 bins (sliding window)
  ↓
Full frame ready → run inference
```

**Sliding Window for Stability**:
```
When frame is ready:
  1. Shift old features: memmove(feat[0], feat[40], 80 bytes)
  2. Append new frame: memcpy(feat[80], new_frame, 40 samples)
```

### Wake Word Detection State Machine

**Config Structure** (loaded from JSON):
```json
{
  "probability_cutoff": 0.5,           // Minimum average probability
  "sliding_window_average_size": 10,   // Window size for averaging
  "min_high_frames": 6,                // Min frames above min_frame_prob
  "min_frame_prob": 0.5,               // Individual frame threshold
  "cooldown_ms": 1500                  // Prevent duplicate triggers
}
```

**Detection Algorithm**:
```
1. Circular buffer: probability_window[config.sliding_window_size]
2. Window filled check: Requires at least N frames of history
3. Per-frame inference: Every 10ms stride
   
Detection trigger when:
  AND(
    window_filled == true,
    millis() - last_detection_ms >= cooldown_ms,
    avg_probability >= probability_cutoff,
    high_frames_count >= min_high_frames
  )
```

Where:
- `avg_probability = mean(probability_window)`
- `high_frames_count = count(probability_window[i] >= min_frame_prob)`

**Cooldown Mechanism**: 
- Prevents multiple triggers within 1500ms
- Resets `probability_window` to zeros after detection

### Main Loop
```
loop():
  captureAudio()                       // I2S read 256 samples
    ↓ (async ringbuffer fill)
  if audio_buffer_pos ≥ 160:
    FrontendProcessSamples()           // Generate spectrogram frame
      ↓
    if feature_frame_count ≥ 3:
      runInference()                   // TFLite invoke
        ↓
      detectWakeword(probability)      // Sliding window logic
        ↓ (if detected)
      LED blink + clear window
```

### Inference Details

**Input Data Type Conversion**:
- Int8: Maps uint16_t feature (0-65535) → int8 (-128 to 127)
- Float: Maps uint16_t → float (0-2560.0 range)

**Output Data Type Support**:
- Uint8: `prob = (raw - zp) * scale`
- Int8: `prob = (raw - zp) * scale`
- Float: Direct use

**Debug Logging**:
```cpp
#define DEBUG_FEATURES 1  // Enables:
- Feature max/sum every 30 frames (300ms)
- Audio amplitude every 300 frames  
- TFLite tensor dimensions and quantization
- Inference input/output every 50 invocations (~500ms)
```

### Memory Management
- PSRAM: Model (~130KB) + tensor_arena (500KB) + var_arena (50KB)
- Heap: Audio buffer (2KB), feature buffer (240 bytes)
- Total: ~700KB PSRAM + minimal heap

### Error Handling
- SD card init fail: `errorBlink()` (200ms LED toggle)
- Model load fail: Print instructions for SD card placement
- Config load fail: Use hardcoded defaults
- IMU init not applicable (audio-only)

## Integration Patterns & Key Takeaways

### Shared Hardware Patterns

| Component | Proto 1 | Proto 2 | Proto 3 |
|-----------|---------|---------|---------|
| Display | ST7789 (SPI) | — | — |
| Microphone | — | Dual INMP441 (I2S0) | Single INMP441 (I2S0) |
| Speaker | — | MAX98357A (I2S1) | — |
| IMU | QMI8658 (I2C) | — | — |
| Button | GPIO 0 (BOOT) | — | — |
| SD Card | Flash FFat | — | SPI SD card |
| LED | GPIO 1 (backlight) | GPIO 1 | GPIO 1 |

### State Machine Patterns
1. **Video rotation**: Debounce-based hysteresis (1000ms)
2. **Wake word detection**: Sliding window with cooldown (1500ms)
3. **Button control**: OneButton debounced events

### Memory Strategies
- **Large assets to PSRAM**: Videos, audio buffers, ML models
- **Small working memory to heap**: Decode buffers, ringbuffers
- `ps_malloc()` instead of `malloc()` for >100KB allocations

### Loop Execution
- **Proto 1**: Decode 1 frame per loop (variable framerate, ~30-60 FPS typical)
- **Proto 2**: Playback in 2048-sample chunks, loops ~15x per second
- **Proto 3**: Process audio continuously, inference every 10ms stride, loops at 10-20 Hz

### Build & Upload
- All require Arduino IDE 2.x or arduino-cli
- Board: ESP32S3 Dev Module
- Partition: 16MB (3MB APP / 9MB FATFS)
- PSRAM: OPI enabled
- Baud: 115200

### File Locations
- **Proto 1**: Video in flash FFat: `/output.mjpeg` (use `upload_to_flash.sh`)
- **Proto 2**: Uses only PSRAM (no external storage)
- **Proto 3**: Model + config on SD card: `/models/hey_daisy.{tflite,json}`

## 1. YAMNet Audio Embedding Prototype (04_yamnet_audio_embedding/)

### Architecture Overview
This is a complete pipeline for extracting 1024-dimensional audio embeddings from 3-5 seconds of audio using Google's YAMNet model with TensorFlow Lite on the ESP32-S3.

### Model Loading & Memory Management

**File Location:** `yamnet_inference.cpp` / `yamnet_inference.h`

**Loading Pattern:**
```cpp
// Step 1: Load from SD card to PSRAM
model_data_ = (uint8_t*)ps_malloc(model_size_);
bytes_read = model_file.read(model_data_, model_size_);  // 167KB-4MB file

// Step 2: Parse TFLite model
model_ = tflite::GetModel(model_data_);
model_->version() == TFLITE_SCHEMA_VERSION;

// Step 3: Allocate tensor arena (400KB fixed)
tensor_arena_ = (uint8_t*)ps_malloc(TENSOR_ARENA_SIZE);  // 400KB in PSRAM

// Step 4: Create interpreter with op resolver
resolver_ = new tflite::MicroMutableOpResolver<10>();
resolver_->AddConv2D();
resolver_->AddDepthwiseConv2D();
resolver_->AddReshape();
resolver_->AddSoftmax();
resolver_->AddFullyConnected();
resolver_->AddMean();
resolver_->AddQuantize();
resolver_->AddDequantize();

interpreter_ = new tflite::MicroInterpreter(model_, *resolver_, tensor_arena_, TENSOR_ARENA_SIZE);
interpreter_->AllocateTensors();
```

**PSRAM Usage:**
- Model weights: 167KB (ST Micro) to 4MB (Google official)
- Tensor arena: 400KB (fixed)
- Total: ~600KB minimum

**Cleanup Pattern:**
```cpp
void end() {
    delete interpreter_;
    delete resolver_;
    free(tensor_arena_);
    free(model_data_);
    vSemaphoreDelete(inference_complete_);
}
```

### Input Preprocessing Pipeline

**Audio Recording (`audio_recorder.cpp`):**
- I2S port: `I2S_NUM_0` (RX mode)
- Configuration: 16-bit stereo @ 16kHz, 32-bit samples from INMP441
- Downmix: Stereo → Mono (simple average)
- Buffer: Records directly to PSRAM
- Time: 3 seconds = 48,000 samples × 2 bytes = 96KB PSRAM

```cpp
// Stereo downmix in real-time during recording
for (int i = 0; i < samples_read && samples_written < num_samples; i += 2) {
    int16_t left = (int16_t)(i2s_buffer_[i] >> 16);
    int16_t right = (int16_t)(i2s_buffer_[i + 1] >> 16);
    buffer[samples_written++] = ((int32_t)left + (int32_t)right) / 2;
}
```

**Mel-Spectrogram Generation (`mel_spectrogram.cpp`):**
- FFT window: 512 samples (25ms @ 16kHz)
- Hop size: 160 samples (10ms @ 16kHz)
- Output: 64 mel bins × 96 frames
- Frequency range: 125Hz - 7500Hz (YAMNet-specific)

**Mel Filterbank Construction:**
```cpp
// Triangular mel filters with Hz→Mel conversion
for (int m = 0; m < MEL_BINS; m++) {
    float left = mel_centers[m];
    float center = mel_centers[m + 1];
    float right = mel_centers[m + 2];
    // Build triangular weights for FFT bins [0...257]
}
```

**ESP-DSP FFT Integration:**
```cpp
dsps_fft2r_init_fc32(NULL, FFT_SIZE);  // Init
dsps_fft2r_fc32(fft_output_, FFT_SIZE);  // 512-point FFT
dsps_bit_rev_fc32(fft_output_, FFT_SIZE);  // Bit reversal
// Power spectrum: |X[k]|^2
```

**Output Format:**
- 64 × 96 = 6,144 float32 values (24.6KB)
- Row-major: [frame][bin]
- Values: log10(sum + 1e-10) = log-mel bins

### Inference Pipeline

**Dual-Core Optimization (`yamnet_inference.cpp`):**
```cpp
bool infer(float* mel_features, float* embeddings) {
    // Main core (Core 0) handles input copy
    float* input_data = input_tensor_->data.f;
    for (int frame = 0; frame < MEL_FRAMES; frame++) {
        for (int bin = 0; bin < MEL_BINS; bin++) {
            input_data[frame * MEL_BINS + bin] = mel_features[frame * MEL_BINS + bin];
        }
    }
    
    // Core 1 runs inference (offloaded)
    xTaskCreatePinnedToCore(
        inferenceTask,
        "yamnet_infer",
        8192,  // Stack size
        &task_params_,
        1,     // Priority
        &inference_task_handle_,
        1      // Core 1
    );
    
    xSemaphoreTake(inference_complete_, portMAX_DELAY);  // Wait for Core 1
}

static void inferenceTask(void* params) {
    TfLiteStatus invoke_status = instance->interpreter_->Invoke();
    xSemaphoreGive(instance->inference_complete_);
    vTaskDelete(NULL);
}
```

**Output Extraction:**
```cpp
// YAMNet-1024 outputs 1024-D embedding directly
float* output_data = output_tensor_->data.f;
int output_size = output_tensor_->dims->data[output_tensor_->dims->size - 1];
for (int i = 0; i < embedding_count; i++) {
    embeddings[i] = output_data[i];
}
```

### Memory Summary (YAMNet)

```
During Operation:
├── Audio buffer: 96 KB (48,000 × int16)
├── Mel-spectrogram: 24.6 KB (6,144 × float32)
├── Embeddings: 4.1 KB (1,024 × float32)
├── Model weights: 167KB - 4MB (SD card loaded to PSRAM)
├── Tensor arena: 400 KB (TFLite working memory)
├── FFT buffers: 8 KB (2 × 512 × float32 + window + filterbank)
└── Total peak: ~600-700 KB (highly compressible - can unload model after inference)

Total time: 10-14 seconds (bottleneck: YAMNet inference at 6-10s)
```

### Dynamic Loading/Unloading Strategy
1. **Load model on demand:** `build_transformer_q8()` from SD card
2. **Use `begin()/end()` pattern:** Clean separation of init/cleanup
3. **PSRAM allocation:** All buffers use `ps_malloc()` for fast access
4. **After inference:** Call `end()` to free everything (model, arena, semaphore)

## 2. LLM Fine-Tuned Inference Prototype (05_llm_finetuned/)

### Architecture Overview
This is a complete int8 quantized LLM inference engine based on llama2.c, adapted for ESP32-S3 with Q8_0 quantization and ESP-DSP SIMD acceleration. Supports 1M-6M parameter models with configurable vocab sizes (512-1024).

### Model Loading & Memory Management

**File Location:** `llm_core.cpp` / `llm_core.h`

**Loading Pattern - Q8_0 Format:**
```cpp
bool build_transformer_q8(Transformer* t, const char* checkpoint_path, int max_seq_len) {
    // Step 1: Validate header
    File file = SD.open(checkpoint_path, FILE_READ);
    uint32_t magic = 0x616b3432;  // "ak42" - Q8_0 format identifier
    uint32_t version = 2;
    
    // Step 2: Read config (256-byte header)
    file.read((uint8_t*)&t->config, sizeof(Config));
    // Config: dim, hidden_dim, n_layers, n_heads, n_kv_heads, vocab_size, seq_len
    file.read(&t->shared_classifier, 1);
    file.read((uint8_t*)&GS, 4);  // Group size (32 or 64)
    
    // Step 3: Load entire model file to PSRAM (16-byte aligned for PIE SIMD)
    t->raw_data = (uint8_t*)heap_caps_aligned_alloc(16, t->file_size, MALLOC_CAP_SPIRAM);
    bytes_read = file.read(t->raw_data, t->file_size);
}
```

**Model Size Examples (3M params @ Q8_0):**
```
- Model file: ~3MB total
- PSRAM loading: Full file into PSRAM (16-byte aligned)
- Header: 256 bytes
- RMS weights: 2 × (n_layers × dim) × 4 bytes
- Token embeddings (int8): vocab_size × dim × 1 byte + scales
- Attention weights (int8): 4 matrices per layer × int8
- FFN weights (int8): 3 matrices per layer × int8
- Classifier: vocab_size × dim × 1 byte + scales (or shared)
```

**Weight Structure - Memory Mapping (no copying):**
```cpp
static void memory_map_weights(TransformerWeights* w, Config* p, void* ptr, uint8_t shared_classifier) {
    // All weights are POINTERS into raw_data, not copies
    // This eliminates redundant memory allocation
    
    float* fptr = (float*)ptr;
    w->rms_att_weight = fptr;  // Direct pointer
    fptr += p->n_layers * p->dim;
    w->rms_ffn_weight = fptr;
    fptr += p->n_layers * p->dim;
    w->rms_final_weight = fptr;
    
    // Quantized tensors (int8 + float scales)
    w->q_tokens = init_quantized_tensors(&ptr, 1, p->vocab_size * p->dim);
    w->wq = init_quantized_tensors(&ptr, p->n_layers, p->dim * (p->n_heads * head_size));
    // ... etc
}

static QuantizedTensor* init_quantized_tensors(void** ptr, int n, int size_each) {
    QuantizedTensor* res = (QuantizedTensor*)malloc(n * sizeof(QuantizedTensor));
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        res[i].q = (int8_t*)p;  // Points into raw_data
        p = (int8_t*)p + size_each;
        res[i].s = (float*)p;   // Scale factors
        p = (float*)p + size_each / GS;
    }
    return res;
}
```

**PSRAM Usage:**
```
Total: ~3-6 MB (depends on model size)
├── Model weights (memory-mapped, not copied): 3-6 MB
├── Token embedding table (dequantized): vocab_size × dim × 4 bytes
│   (e.g., 1024 vocab × 128 dim = 512KB)
├── Run state activation buffers: ~2-3 MB
│   ├── x, xb, xb2: 3 × dim × 4 bytes
│   ├── hb, hb2: 2 × hidden_dim × 4 bytes
│   ├── q, att, logits: various
│   ├── KV cache: 2 × n_layers × seq_len × kv_dim × 4 bytes (LARGEST)
│   │  (e.g., 4 layers × 256 pos × 64 kv_dim × 4 = 256KB per layer)
│   └── Quantized buffers (int8): dim + hidden_dim (16-byte aligned for SIMD)
└── RoPE cache: 2 × seq_len × (dim / n_heads / 2) × 4 bytes
    (e.g., 256 × 16 × 4 = 16KB)
```

**Cleanup Pattern:**
```cpp
void free_transformer(Transformer* t) {
    free(t->raw_data);  // Model file
    free(t->weights.token_embedding_table);  // Dequantized embeddings
    free(t->rope_cos);
    free(t->rope_sin);
    free(t->weights.q_tokens);  // QuantizedTensor structs
    free(t->weights.wq);
    // ... etc
    free_run_state(&t->state);  // All activation buffers
}
```

bool build_tokenizer(Tokenizer* t, const char* tokenizer_path, int vocab_size) {
    // From SD card binary format
    File file = SD.open(tokenizer_path, FILE_READ);
    
    // Read max token length
    file.read((uint8_t*)&t->max_token_length, sizeof(int));
    
    // Read vocab (vocab_size entries)
    for (int i = 0; i < vocab_size; i++) {

        t->vocab[i] = (char*)malloc(len + 1);
        file.read((uint8_t*)t->vocab[i], len);
    }
}

**Sampling Strategies:**
```cpp
void build_sampler(Sampler* sampler, int vocab_size, float temperature, float topp, unsigned long long rng_seed) {
    sampler->vocab_size = vocab_size;
    sampler->probindex = (ProbIndex*)malloc(vocab_size * sizeof(ProbIndex));
    sampler->temperature = temperature;
    sampler->topp = topp;
    sampler->rng_state = rng_seed;
}

int sample(Sampler* sampler, v4sf* logits) {
    // 1. Apply temperature scaling
    dsps_mulc_f32_ae32(logits, logits, vocab_size, 1.0f / temperature, 1, 1);
    
    // 2. Softmax
    softmax_sampling(logits, vocab_size);
    
    // 3. Top-p filtering (nucleus sampling)
    int sample_topp(logits, vocab_size, topp, probindex, random_f32());
}
```

### Inference Pipeline (Forward Pass)

**File Location:** `llm_core.cpp` - `forward()` function

**Token Embedding:**
```cpp
float* content_row = w->token_embedding_table + token * dim;  // Precomputed, not quantized
memcpy(s->x, content_row, dim * sizeof(float));
```

**Transformer Layers (per-layer operations):**
```cpp
for (int l = 0; l < p->n_layers; l++) {
    // 1. RMS normalization (with ESP-DSP SIMD)
    rmsnorm(s->xb, s->x, w->rms_att_weight + l * dim, dim);
    
    // 2. Quantize activation: float → int8 per-group
    quantize(&s->xq, s->xb, dim);
    
    // 3. Attention projections (quantized matmul)
    matmul_q8(s->q, &s->xq, &w->wq[l], dim, dim);  // Query
    matmul_q8(s->k, &s->xq, &w->wk[l], dim, kv_dim);  // Key
    matmul_q8(s->v, &s->xq, &w->wv[l], dim, kv_dim);  // Value
    
    // 4. RoPE (Rotary Position Embedding) with cached sin/cos
    // Lookup precomputed RoPE values instead of runtime trig
    float* cos_ptr = transformer->rope_cos + pos * half_head;
    float* sin_ptr = transformer->rope_sin + pos * half_head;
    for (int i = 0; i < dim; i += 2) {
        // Apply 2D rotation
    }
    
    // 5. Multi-head attention with KV cache
    for (int h = 0; h < p->n_heads; h++) {
        // Score: Q @ K^T / sqrt(d_k) [with SIMD dot product]
        dsps_dotprod_f32_aes3(q, k, &score, head_size);
        
        // Softmax over sequence positions
        // Aggregate: sum(attention * V) [with SIMD]
        dsps_mulc_f32_ae32(v, s->xb2, head_size, a, 1, 1);  // a * v
        dsps_add_f32_ae32(xb, s->xb2, xb, head_size, 1, 1, 1);  // xb += temp
    }
    
    // 6. Output projection (quantized)
    matmul_q8(s->xb2, &s->xq, &w->wo[l], dim, dim);
    
    // 7. Residual connection (with SIMD)
    dsps_add_f32_ae32(s->x, s->xb2, s->x, dim, 1, 1, 1);
    
    // 8. FFN: RMS norm
    rmsnorm(s->xb, s->x, w->rms_ffn_weight + l * dim, dim);
    
    // 9. FFN: Gate and projection (quantized)
    quantize(&s->xq, s->xb, dim);
    matmul_q8(s->hb, &s->xq, &w->w1[l], dim, hidden_dim);   // Gate
    matmul_q8(s->hb2, &s->xq, &w->w3[l], dim, hidden_dim);  // Up
    
    // 10. SwiGLU with fast sigmoid
    for (int i = 0; i < hidden_dim; i += 4) {
        v0 *= 1.0f / (1.0f + expf(-v0));  // sigmoid
        s->hb[i] = v0 * s->hb2[i];  // Gate multiply
    }
    
    // 11. FFN output (quantized)
    quantize(&s->hq, s->hb, hidden_dim);
    matmul_q8(s->xb, &s->hq, &w->w2[l], hidden_dim, dim);
    
    // 12. Residual
    dsps_add_f32_ae32(s->x, s->xb, s->x, dim, 1, 1, 1);
}

// Final norm and classifier
rmsnorm(s->x, s->x, w->rms_final_weight, dim);
quantize(&s->xq, s->x, dim);
matmul_q8(s->logits, &s->xq, w->wcls, dim, p->vocab_size);  // logits
return s->logits;
```

### Quantization System (Q8_0 Format)

**Dequantization (weights → activations):**
```cpp
void dequantize(QuantizedTensor *qx, float* x, int n) {
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        x[i] = qx->q[i] * qx->s[i / GS];  // qx->s is per-group scale
    }
}
```

**Per-Group Quantization (activations → weights):**
```cpp
void quantize(QuantizedTensor *qx, float* x, int n) {
    int num_groups = n / GS;  // GS = 32 or 64
    float Q_MAX = 127.0f;
    
    for (int group = 0; group < num_groups; group++) {
        float* gx = x + group * GS;
        int8_t* gq = qx->q + group * GS;
        
        // Find max |x| in group
        float wmax = 0.0f;
        for (int i = 0; i < GS; i += 4) {
            if (fabsf(gx[i]) > wmax) wmax = fabsf(gx[i]);
            // ... etc
        }
        
        // Compute scale and quantize
        float scale = wmax / Q_MAX;
        qx->s[group] = scale;
        float inv_scale = Q_MAX / wmax;
        
        for (int i = 0; i < GS; i += 4) {
            gq[i] = (int8_t)(gx[i] * inv_scale + 0.5f - (gx[i] < 0));
            // ... etc
        }
    }
}
```

### SIMD Quantized Matmul (Q8_0)

**PIE SIMD int8 Dot Product (Core operation):**
```cpp
static inline int32_t dotprod_s8_simd(const int8_t* a, const int8_t* b, int len) {
    // Uses ESP32-S3 PIE vector instructions
    // Processes 16 int8 pairs per iteration (40-bit accumulator)
    
    asm volatile(
        "wur.accx_0 %[zero]\n"        // Clear accumulator
        "wur.accx_1 %[zero]\n"
        
        "loopnez %[chunks], 1f\n"
        "ee.vld.128.ip q0, %[a], 16\n"    // Load 16 int8s
        "ee.vld.128.ip q1, %[b], 16\n"    // Load 16 int8s
        "ee.vmulas.s8.accx q0, q1\n"      // MAC: accx += sum(q0[i] * q1[i])
        "1:\n"
        
        "rur.accx_0 %[result]\n"      // Read accumulator
    );
}

void matmul_q8(float* xout, QuantizedTensor* x, QuantizedTensor* w, int n, int d) {
    // Matrix: W[d×n] @ x[n] → xout[d]
    for (int i = 0; i < d; i++) {
        float val = 0.0f;
        for (int j = 0; j <= n - GS; j += GS) {
            // SIMD dot product for group
            int32_t ival = dotprod_s8_simd(x->q + j, w->q + in + j, GS);
            
            // Scale by per-group scales
            val += (float)ival * w->s[(in + j) / GS] * x->s[j / GS];
        }
        xout[i] = val;
    }
}
```

**Performance:** 3x speedup vs. scalar int8 matmul (from recent commits)

### Configuration & Streaming

**File Location:** `05_llm_finetuned.ino`

**JSON Config Loading:**
```cpp
struct LLMConfig {
    char model_path[64];      // e.g., "/models/ajv009_3M_1024TK_q80.bin"
    char tokenizer_path[64];  // e.g., "/models/ajv009_1024TK.bin"
    float temperature;        // 0.8
    float topp;              // 0.9
    int max_tokens;          // 128
    int max_seq_len;         // Override model's seq_len (0 = use model default)
};

bool loadConfig(const char* path) {
    StaticJsonDocument<512> doc;
    deserializeJson(doc, f);
    strlcpy(config.model_path, doc["model"] | DEFAULT_MODEL, sizeof(config.model_path));
    config.temperature = doc["temperature"] | DEFAULT_TEMPERATURE;
    // ... etc
}
```

**Prompt Wrapping:**
```cpp
String wrapPrompt(const char* userInput) {
    return String("<|user|>") + userInput + "<|assistant|>";
}

bool isEndToken(const char* piece) {
    return piece && strstr(piece, "<|end|>") != nullptr;
}
```

**Streaming Generation:**
```cpp
void generate(const char* prompt, int steps) {
    // Encode wrapped prompt
    int num_prompt_tokens = 0;
    encode(&tokenizer, (char*)wrapped.c_str(), 0, 0, prompt_tokens, &num_prompt_tokens);
    
    // Generation loop (autoregressive)
    int token = prompt_tokens[0];
    int pos = 0;
    
    while (pos < steps) {
        float* logits = forward(&transformer, token, pos);  // Single token forward pass
        
        if (pos < num_prompt_tokens - 1) {
            // Still processing prompt (no sampling)
            next = prompt_tokens[pos + 1];
        } else {
            // Sample from logits
            next = sample(&sampler, logits);
        }
        
        // Decode and stream
        char* piece = decode(&tokenizer, token, next);
        if (isEndToken(piece)) break;
        Serial.print(piece);  // Stream output character-by-character
        
        token = next;
        pos++;
    }
    
    // Print performance: tokens/second
}
```

### Memory Summary (LLM)

```
Example: 3M-param model @ Q8_0, 1024 vocab, 128 dim, 4 layers, seq_len=256

Startup (load phase):
├── Model file (3MB): loaded to PSRAM (16-byte aligned)
├── Token embeddings (dequantized): 1024 × 128 × 4 = 512 KB
├── Run state (activations):
│   ├── x, xb, xb2: 3 × 128 × 4 = 1.5 KB
│   ├── hb, hb2: 2 × 512 × 4 = 4 KB
│   ├── KV cache: 2 × 4 × 256 × 64 × 4 = 256 KB (LARGEST activations)
│   ├── Quantized buffers: 128 + 512 (16-byte aligned)
│   └── Various: q, att, logits, scales
├── Tokenizer: 512 KB (vocab + scoring)
├── Sampler: ~64 KB (ProbIndex array)
└── RoPE cache: 16 KB
Total: ~4.5 - 5.5 MB PSRAM

Runtime (per token inference):
├── Forward pass: Uses KV cache (no redundant computation)
├── Memory bandwidth: Model weights are read-only (2-3MB accessed)
├── Inference time: ~100-500ms per token (depends on batch)
```

### Dynamic Loading/Unloading Strategy

```cpp
// Load on startup in setup()
build_transformer_q8(&transformer, config.model_path, config.max_seq_len);
build_tokenizer(&tokenizer, config.tokenizer_path, transformer.config.vocab_size);
build_sampler(&sampler, transformer.config.vocab_size, config.temperature, config.topp, seed);

// Unload (if needed)
free_transformer(&transformer);
free_tokenizer(&tokenizer);
free_sampler(&sampler);

// Re-load different model
build_transformer_q8(&transformer, "/models/different_model.bin", 0);
```

## 3. Comparative Analysis

| Aspect | YAMNet (Embedding) | LLM (Generation) |
|--------|-------------------|------------------|
| **Model Size** | 167KB - 4MB | 3-6 MB |
| **PSRAM Peak** | ~600-700 KB | ~4.5-5.5 MB |
| **Input Format** | 64×96 mel-spectrogram | Token IDs |
| **Output Format** | 1024-D float vector | Logits (vocab_size) |
| **Inference Time** | 6-10 seconds | 100-500ms per token |
| **Quantization** | Model-provided (int8) | Q8_0 (per-group) |
| **SIMD** | ESP-DSP FFT | PIE int8 matmul |
| **Dual-Core** | Core 0 input, Core 1 inference | Single core (Core 0) |
| **Streaming** | One-shot (produces embedding) | Streaming (token-by-token) |
| **KV Cache** | None | 256 KB (per layer) |

---

## 4. Key Patterns for Dynamic Model Management

### Pattern 1: Check Memory Before Loading
```cpp
if (total_needed > ESP.getFreePsram()) {
    Serial.println("ERROR: Not enough PSRAM for model!");
    return false;
}
```

### Pattern 2: Load from SD (Streaming)
- YAMNet: Entire model to PSRAM buffer, then parse
- LLM: Entire model to PSRAM (16-byte aligned), then memory-map (no copy)

### Pattern 3: Lazy Initialization
- Tokenizer: Builds sorted vocab on first `encode()` call
- Sampler: Allocates ProbIndex array once

### Pattern 4: Clean Separation
```cpp
bool begin();      // Load + initialize
bool infer/forward();  // Run inference
void end();        // Cleanup all allocations
```

### Pattern 5: Per-Group Quantization
- Activations quantized before each layer's matmul
- Scales stored per-group (not per-element) to save memory

---

## 5. Recommendations for Larger Applications

1. **Pre-allocate model pool:** Reserve PSRAM space for multiple models
2. **Implement model swap:** Load Model A, inference, unload, load Model B
3. **Streaming output:** Both support partial output (embeddings are single tensor, LLM is token-by-token)
4. **Memory-map weights:** Like LLM does—avoid redundant copies
5. **Lazy tokenizer builds:** Don't require sorted vocab upfront
6. **Config-driven selection:** Use JSON on SD card to choose model at runtime

     2→ * ESP32-S3-LCD-2 MJPEG Video Player with Gyro-based Auto-Rotation
     3→ * Plays MJPEG video from flash memory in infinite loop
     4→ * BOOT button (pin 0):
     5→ *   - Click: Toggle pause/play
     6→ *   - Long press: Power off/on (blank screen + backlight off)
     7→ * Auto-rotation: Screen rotates 180° when device orientation changes
     8→ ******************************************************************************/
     9→
    10→#include <FFat.h>

    24→#define IMU_ADDRESS 0x6B
    25→#define I2C_SDA 48
    26→#define I2C_SCL 47

    28→// IMU objects
    29→QMI8658 IMU;

    32→
    33→// Memory stream for PSRAM playback
    34→class MemoryStream : public Stream {
    35→  uint8_t *buf;
    36→  size_t sz, pos;
    37→public:
    38→  MemoryStream(uint8_t *b, size_t s) : buf(b), sz(s), pos(0) {}
    39→  int available() override { return sz - pos; }
    40→  int read() override { return (pos < sz) ? buf[pos++] : -1; }
    41→  int peek() override { return (pos < sz) ? buf[pos] : -1; }
    42→  size_t readBytes(char *b, size_t len) override {
    43→    size_t n = min(len, sz - pos);
    44→    memcpy(b, buf + pos, n);
    45→    pos += n;
    46→    return n;
    47→  }
    48→  void reset() { pos = 0; }
    49→  size_t write(uint8_t) override { return 0; }
    50→  void flush() override {}
    51→};
    52→
    53→// Orientation manager with debounced rotation detection
    54→class OrientationManager {
    55→  const float THRESHOLD = 0.5;           // Hysteresis threshold (±0.5g)
    56→  const unsigned long DEBOUNCE_MS = 1000; // 1 second stability required
    57→  const unsigned long POLL_INTERVAL_MS = 50; // Poll at 20Hz
    58→
    59→  uint8_t currentRotation;    // Stable rotation: 1 (USB right) or 3 (USB left)
    60→  uint8_t pendingRotation;    // Candidate rotation during debounce (0 = none)
    61→  unsigned long debounceStartTime;
    62→  unsigned long lastPollTime;
    63→  bool rotationJustChanged;   // One-shot flag for change detection
    64→  bool imuAvailable;
    65→
    66→public:
    67→  OrientationManager() : currentRotation(1), pendingRotation(0),
    68→                         debounceStartTime(0), lastPollTime(0),
    69→                         rotationJustChanged(false), imuAvailable(true) {}
    70→
    71→  void setImuAvailable(bool available) {
    72→    imuAvailable = available;
    73→  }
    74→
    75→  void update() {
    76→    if (!imuAvailable) return;
    77→
    78→    unsigned long now = millis();
    79→    if (now - lastPollTime < POLL_INTERVAL_MS) return;
    80→    lastPollTime = now;
    81→
    82→    // Read accelerometer
    83→    IMU.update();
    84→    IMU.getAccel(&accelData);
    85→    float accelY = accelData.accelY;
    86→
    87→    // Determine desired rotation based on accelY
    88→    uint8_t desiredRotation = 0;
    89→    if (accelY > THRESHOLD) {
    90→      desiredRotation = 1;  // USB on right (normal)
    91→    } else if (accelY < -THRESHOLD) {
    92→      desiredRotation = 3;  // USB on left (180° flip)
    93→    } else {
    94→      desiredRotation = currentRotation; // Hysteresis zone - keep current
    95→    }
    96→
    97→    // State machine logic
    98→    if (desiredRotation == currentRotation) {
    99→      // Orientation matches current stable state
   100→      pendingRotation = 0; // Cancel any pending transition
   101→    } else if (pendingRotation == 0) {
   102→      // Start new transition
   103→      pendingRotation = desiredRotation;
   104→      debounceStartTime = now;
   105→    } else if (pendingRotation == desiredRotation) {
   106→      // Transition in progress, check if debounce time elapsed
   107→      if (now - debounceStartTime >= DEBOUNCE_MS) {
   108→        // Commit rotation change
   109→        currentRotation = pendingRotation;
   110→        pendingRotation = 0;
   111→        rotationJustChanged = true;
   112→      }
   113→    } else {
   114→      // Desired rotation changed during debounce - restart
   115→      pendingRotation = desiredRotation;
   116→      debounceStartTime = now;
   117→    }
   118→  }
   119→
   120→  uint8_t getRotation() {
   121→    return currentRotation;
   122→  }
   123→
   124→  bool hasChanged() {
   125→    if (rotationJustChanged) {
   126→      rotationJustChanged = false; // Clear one-shot flag
   127→      return true;
   128→    }
   129→    return false;
   130→  }
   131→};

   188→    display = new Arduino_ST7789(bus, -1, 1, true, 240, 320);
   189→    if (!display->begin()) return false;
   190→    pinMode(LCD_BL, OUTPUT);
   191→    digitalWrite(LCD_BL, HIGH);
   192→    display->fillScreen(BLACK);

   194→    // Mount flash and load video

   196→    File f = FFat.open("/output.mjpeg", "r");

   205→    f.close();

   211→  }

   218→    } else {
   219→      stream->reset();
   220→      decoder.reset();
   221→    }
   222→  }

   266→    if (num_samples_read < audio_buffer_pos) {
   267→      memmove(audio_buffer, audio_buffer + num_samples_read,
   268→              (audio_buffer_pos - num_samples_read) * sizeof(int16_t));
   269→    }
   270→    audio_buffer_pos -= num_samples_read;
   271→
   272→    if (frontend_output.size == FEATURE_BINS) {
   273→      if (feature_frame_count >= FEATURE_FRAMES) {
   274→        memmove(feature_buffer, feature_buffer + FEATURE_BINS,
   275→                (FEATURE_FRAMES - 1) * FEATURE_BINS * sizeof(uint16_t));
   276→        feature_frame_count = FEATURE_FRAMES - 1;
   277→      }
   278→
   279→      memcpy(feature_buffer + feature_frame_count * FEATURE_BINS,
   280→             frontend_output.values, FEATURE_BINS * sizeof(uint16_t));
   281→      feature_frame_count++;
   282→
   283→      if (feature_frame_count >= FEATURE_FRAMES) {
   284→#if DEBUG_FEATURES
   285→        static int debug_count = 0;
   286→        if (++debug_count >= 30) {
   287→          debug_count = 0;
   288→          uint32_t energy = 0;
   289→          uint16_t max_feat = 0;
   290→          for (int i = 0; i < FEATURE_FRAMES * FEATURE_BINS; i++) {
   291→            energy += feature_buffer[i];
   292→            if (feature_buffer[i] > max_feat) max_feat = feature_buffer[i];
   293→          }
   294→          Serial.printf("Features: max=%u, sum=%lu\n", max_feat, energy);
   295→        }
   296→#endif
   297→        float prob = runInference();
   298→
   299→        if (detectWakeword(prob)) {
   300→          Serial.printf("\n>>> %s DETECTED! <<<\n\n", config.wake_word);
   301→          digitalWrite(LED_PIN, HIGH);
   302→          delay(500);
   303→          digitalWrite(LED_PIN, LOW);
   304→
   305→          for (int i = 0; i < config.sliding_window_size; i++) {
   306→            probability_window[i] = 0.0f;
   307→          }
   308→          window_filled = false;
   309→        }
   310→      }
   311→    }
   312→  }
   313→}

   319→bool loadConfig(const char* path) {
   320→  File f = SD.open(path);

   326→  // Parse JSON

   330→
   331→  if (error) {
   332→    Serial.printf("JSON parse error: %s\n", error.c_str());
   333→    return false;
   334→  }
   335→
   336→  // Load wake word name
   337→  const char* wake_word = doc["wake_word"] | "Hey Daisy";
   338→  strncpy(config.wake_word, wake_word, sizeof(config.wake_word) - 1);
   339→
   340→  // Load detection parameters from "micro" object
   341→  JsonObject micro = doc["micro"];
   342→  if (micro) {
   343→    config.probability_cutoff = micro["probability_cutoff"] | 0.5f;
   344→    config.sliding_window_size = micro["sliding_window_average_size"] | 10;
   345→    config.min_high_frames = micro["min_high_frames"] | 6;
   346→    config.min_frame_prob = micro["min_frame_prob"] | 0.5f;
   347→    config.cooldown_ms = micro["cooldown_ms"] | 1500;
   348→  }
   349→
   350→  // Clamp sliding window size to max
   351→  if (config.sliding_window_size > MAX_SLIDING_WINDOW) {
   352→    config.sliding_window_size = MAX_SLIDING_WINDOW;
   353→  }
   354→
   355→  Serial.printf("Config loaded: %s\n", path);
   356→  return true;
   357→}

   363→bool initInterpreter() {
   364→  const tflite::Model* model = tflite::GetModel(model_data);

   367→                  model->version(), TFLITE_SCHEMA_VERSION);

   369→  }
   370→
   371→  var_allocator = tflite::MicroAllocator::Create(var_arena, VAR_ARENA_SIZE);
   372→  if (!var_allocator) {
   373→    Serial.println("Failed to create var allocator");
   374→    return false;
   375→  }
   376→
   377→  resource_vars = tflite::MicroResourceVariables::Create(var_allocator, MAX_RESOURCE_VARS);
   378→  if (!resource_vars) {
   379→    Serial.println("Failed to create resource variables");
   380→    return false;
   381→  }
   382→
   383→  static tflite::MicroInterpreter static_interpreter(
   384→      model, resolver, tensor_arena, TENSOR_ARENA_SIZE, resource_vars);
   385→  interpreter = &static_interpreter;
   386→
   387→  if (interpreter->AllocateTensors() != kTfLiteOk) {
   388→    Serial.println("AllocateTensors failed");
   389→    return false;
   390→  }
   391→
   392→  input_tensor = interpreter->input(0);

   395→  if (!input_tensor || !output_tensor) {
   396→    Serial.println("Failed to get tensors");
   397→    return false;
   398→  }
   399→
   400→  return true;
   401→}

   477→bool captureAudio() {
   478→  int space_available = AUDIO_BUFFER_SIZE - audio_buffer_pos;
   479→  if (space_available < 256) {
   480→    return true;
   481→  }
   482→
   483→  int samples_to_read = min(256, space_available);
   484→  size_t bytes_read;
   485→  if (i2s_read(I2S_NUM_0, i2s_buffer, samples_to_read * 4, &bytes_read, 10) != ESP_OK) {
   486→    return false;
   487→  }
   488→
   489→  int samples = bytes_read / 4;
   490→
   491→  static int audio_debug = 0;
   492→  int32_t max_sample = 0;
   493→
   494→  for (int i = 0; i < samples; i++) {
   495→    int32_t sample = i2s_buffer[i] >> 14;
   496→    audio_buffer[audio_buffer_pos++] = constrain(sample, -32768, 32767);
   497→    if (abs(sample) > max_sample) max_sample = abs(sample);
   498→  }
   499→
   500→#if DEBUG_FEATURES
   501→  if (++audio_debug >= 300) {
   502→    audio_debug = 0;
   503→    Serial.printf("Audio: amp=%ld, buf=%d\n", max_sample, audio_buffer_pos);
   504→  }
   505→#endif
   506→
   507→  return true;
   508→}

   510→//=============================================================================
   511→// INFERENCE
   512→//=============================================================================
   513→
   514→float runInference() {
   515→  int total_features = FEATURE_FRAMES * FEATURE_BINS;
   516→
   517→  static bool printed_params = false;
   518→  if (!printed_params) {
   519→    printed_params = true;
   520→    Serial.printf("\n=== INFERENCE DEBUG ===\n");
   521→    Serial.printf("Input type=%d, scale=%.6f, zp=%d\n",
   522→      input_tensor->type, input_tensor->params.scale, input_tensor->params.zero_point);
   523→    Serial.printf("Output type=%d, scale=%.6f, zp=%d\n",
   524→      output_tensor->type, output_tensor->params.scale, output_tensor->params.zero_point);
   525→    Serial.printf("Input bytes=%d, Output bytes=%d\n",
   526→      input_tensor->bytes, output_tensor->bytes);
   527→  }
   528→
   529→  if (input_tensor->type == kTfLiteInt8) {
   530→    int8_t* input_data = input_tensor->data.int8;
   531→    for (int i = 0; i < total_features; i++) {
   532→      int32_t scaled = ((int32_t)feature_buffer[i] * 256 + 333) / 666 - 128;
   533→      input_data[i] = constrain(scaled, -128, 127);
   534→    }
   535→
   536→    static int input_debug = 0;
   537→    if (++input_debug == 50) {
   538→      Serial.printf("Input[0-5]: %d,%d,%d,%d,%d,%d\n",
   539→        input_data[0], input_data[1], input_data[2],
   540→        input_data[3], input_data[4], input_data[5]);
   541→    }
   542→  } else {
   543→    float* input_data = input_tensor->data.f;
   544→    for (int i = 0; i < total_features; i++) {
   545→      input_data[i] = feature_buffer[i] / 25.6f;
   546→    }
   547→  }
   548→
   549→  if (interpreter->Invoke() != kTfLiteOk) {
   550→    Serial.println("Invoke failed");
   551→    return 0.0f;
   552→  }
   553→
   554→  float probability;
   555→  static int out_debug = 0;
   556→
   557→  if (output_tensor->type == kTfLiteUInt8) {
   558→    uint8_t output_value = output_tensor->data.uint8[0];
   559→    probability = (output_value - output_tensor->params.zero_point) *
   560→                  output_tensor->params.scale;
   561→    if (++out_debug == 50) {
   562→      Serial.printf("Raw output uint8=%u, prob=%.4f\n", output_value, probability);
   563→    }
   564→  } else if (output_tensor->type == kTfLiteInt8) {
   565→    int8_t output_value = output_tensor->data.int8[0];
   566→    probability = (output_value - output_tensor->params.zero_point) *
   567→                  output_tensor->params.scale;
   568→    if (++out_debug == 50) {
   569→      Serial.printf("Raw output int8=%d, prob=%.4f\n", output_value, probability);
   570→    }
   571→  } else {
   572→    probability = output_tensor->data.f[0];
   573→    if (++out_debug == 50) {
   574→      Serial.printf("Raw output float=%.4f\n", probability);
   575→    }
   576→  }
   577→
   578→  return probability;
   579→}
   580→
   581→//=============================================================================
   582→// DETECTION
   583→//=============================================================================
   584→
   585→bool detectWakeword(float probability) {
   586→  probability_window[window_pos] = probability;
   587→  window_pos = (window_pos + 1) % config.sliding_window_size;
   588→
   589→  if (window_pos == 0) {
   590→    window_filled = true;
   591→  }
   592→
   593→  if (!window_filled) {
   594→    return false;
   595→  }
   596→
   597→  if (millis() - last_detection_ms < (unsigned long)config.cooldown_ms) {
   598→    return false;
   599→  }
   600→
   601→  float avg = 0.0f;
   602→  int high_frames = 0;
   603→  for (int i = 0; i < config.sliding_window_size; i++) {
   604→    avg += probability_window[i];
   605→    if (probability_window[i] >= config.min_frame_prob) {
   606→      high_frames++;
   607→    }
   608→  }
   609→  avg /= config.sliding_window_size;
   610→
   611→  static int log_count = 0;
   612→  if (probability > 0.01f || ++log_count >= 100) {
   613→    Serial.printf("prob: %.4f, avg: %.4f, high: %d/%d\n",
   614→                  probability, avg, high_frames, config.sliding_window_size);
   615→    log_count = 0;
   616→  }
   617→
   618→  if (avg >= config.probability_cutoff && high_frames >= config.min_high_frames) {
   619→    last_detection_ms = millis();
   620→    return true;
   621→  }
   622→  return false;
   623→}
   624→
   625→//=============================================================================
   626→// UTILITY
   627→//=============================================================================
   628→
   629→void errorBlink() {
   630→  while (1) {
   631→    digitalWrite(LED_PIN, !digitalRead(LED_PIN));
   632→    delay(200);
   633→  }
   634→}

     8→ * Hardware:

    10→ * INMP441 Microphones (I2S0 RX):

    23→ * Behavior:

   180→  normalizeAudio();
   181→  Serial.println();
   182→
   183→  Serial.println("========================================");
   184→  Serial.println("Starting playback loop...");
   185→  Serial.println("========================================\n");
   186→
   187→  digitalWrite(LED_PIN, HIGH);
   188→}
   189→
   190→void loop() {
   191→  playMonoBuffer();
   192→}
   193→
   194→bool recordStereoToPSRAM() {
   195→  uint32_t samples_written = 0;
   196→  uint32_t last_percent = 0;
   197→  unsigned long start_time = millis();
   198→
   199→  while (samples_written < STEREO_SAMPLES) {
   200→    // Blink LED
   201→    if ((millis() / 200) % 2 == 0) {
   202→      digitalWrite(LED_PIN, HIGH);
   203→    } else {
   204→      digitalWrite(LED_PIN, LOW);
   205→    }
   206→
   207→    // Read I2S
   208→    size_t bytes_read = 0;
   209→    if (i2s_read(I2S_NUM_0, i2s_buffer, BUFFER_SIZE * sizeof(int32_t),
   210→                 &bytes_read, portMAX_DELAY) != ESP_OK) {
   211→      return false;
   212→    }
   213→
   214→    // Convert and store
   215→    int samples_read = bytes_read / sizeof(int32_t);
   216→    for (int i = 0; i < samples_read && samples_written < STEREO_SAMPLES; i++) {
   217→      stereo_buffer[samples_written++] = (int16_t)(i2s_buffer[i] >> 16);
   218→    }
   219→
   220→    // Progress
   221→    uint32_t percent = (samples_written * 100) / STEREO_SAMPLES;
   222→    if (percent != last_percent && percent % 10 == 0) {
   223→      Serial.printf("Progress: %u%% (%u / %u samples)\n",
   224→                    percent, samples_written, STEREO_SAMPLES);
   225→      last_percent = percent;
   226→    }
   227→  }
   228→
   229→  Serial.printf("\nRecorded: %u samples in %lu ms\n", samples_written, millis() - start_time);
   230→  return true;
   231→}
   232→
   233→void downmixHybrid() {
   234→  float left_energy = 0.0f;
   235→  float right_energy = 0.0f;
   236→  const float ENERGY_DECAY = 0.95f;
   237→  const float MIN_WEIGHT = 0.30f;  // Minimum 30% per channel
   238→  const float MAX_WEIGHT = 0.70f;  // Maximum 70% per channel
   239→  const float GAIN_BOOST = 4.0f;   // 4x volume boost (compensates for 9dB hardware gain)
   240→
   241→  for (uint32_t i = 0; i < MONO_SAMPLES; i++) {
   242→    int16_t left = stereo_buffer[i * 2];
   243→    int16_t right = stereo_buffer[i * 2 + 1];
   244→
   245→    // Track energy of each channel
   246→    left_energy = left_energy * ENERGY_DECAY + abs(left) * (1.0f - ENERGY_DECAY);
   247→    right_energy = right_energy * ENERGY_DECAY + abs(right) * (1.0f - ENERGY_DECAY);
   248→
   249→    // Calculate raw weights
   250→    float total_energy = left_energy + right_energy;
   251→    float left_weight = (total_energy > 0) ? (left_energy / total_energy) : 0.5f;
   252→
   253→    // Constrain to 30%-70% range
   254→    if (left_weight < MIN_WEIGHT) left_weight = MIN_WEIGHT;
   255→    if (left_weight > MAX_WEIGHT) left_weight = MAX_WEIGHT;
   256→
   257→    float right_weight = 1.0f - left_weight;
   258→
   259→    // Weighted mix with gain boost and clipping protection
   260→    int32_t mixed = (int32_t)(left * left_weight + right * right_weight) * GAIN_BOOST;
   261→    if (mixed > 32767) mixed = 32767;
   262→    if (mixed < -32768) mixed = -32768;
   263→    mono_buffer[i] = (int16_t)mixed;
   264→  }
   265→}
   266→
   267→void normalizeAudio() {
   268→  // Find peak level in recording
   269→  int16_t peak = 0;
   270→  for (uint32_t i = 0; i < MONO_SAMPLES; i++) {
   271→    int16_t abs_val = abs(mono_buffer[i]);
   272→    if (abs_val > peak) peak = abs_val;
   273→  }
   274→
   275→  Serial.printf("Peak level: %d / 32767 (%.1f%%)\n", peak, (peak * 100.0f) / 32767.0f);
   276→
   277→  // Calculate normalization gain to maximize volume
   278→  if (peak > 0) {
   279→    float norm_gain = 32000.0f / peak;  // Leave small headroom (32000 instead of 32767)
   280→
   281→    // Limit max boost to 8x to avoid amplifying noise too much
   282→    if (norm_gain > 8.0f) norm_gain = 8.0f;
   283→
   284→    Serial.printf("Applying normalization: %.2fx gain\n", norm_gain);
   285→
   286→    // Apply normalization
   287→    for (uint32_t i = 0; i < MONO_SAMPLES; i++) {
   288→      int32_t normalized = (int32_t)(mono_buffer[i] * norm_gain);
   289→      if (normalized > 32767) normalized = 32767;
   290→      if (normalized < -32768) normalized = -32768;
   291→      mono_buffer[i] = (int16_t)normalized;
   292→    }
   293→  } else {
   294→    Serial.println("WARNING: Recording is silent (peak = 0)!");
   295→  }
   296→}
   297→
   298→void playMonoBuffer() {
   299→  size_t bytes_written = 0;
   300→  static unsigned long last_print = 0;
   301→
   302→  // Play entire mono buffer
   303→  for (uint32_t i = 0; i < MONO_SAMPLES; i += BUFFER_SIZE) {
   304→    uint32_t samples_to_write = min((uint32_t)BUFFER_SIZE, MONO_SAMPLES - i);
   305→
   306→    i2s_write(I2S_NUM_1, &mono_buffer[i], samples_to_write * sizeof(int16_t),
   307→              &bytes_written, portMAX_DELAY);
   308→
   309→    // Print status every ~2 seconds
   310→    if (millis() - last_print > 2000) {
   311→      Serial.printf("Playing... sample %u / %u\n", i, MONO_SAMPLES);
   312→      last_print = millis();
   313→    }
   314→  }
   315→
   316→  Serial.println("Playback complete, looping...\n");
   317→}
   318→
   319→void error_blink() {
   320→  while(1) {
   321→    digitalWrite(LED_PIN, !digitalRead(LED_PIN));
   322→    delay(200);
   323→  }
   324→}
   325→

   192→            start_time = millis();
   193→        }
   194→    }
   195→
   196→    // Print performance stats
   197→    if (generated > 0 && start_time > 0) {
   198→        unsigned long elapsed = millis() - start_time;
   199→        float tokens_per_sec = (float)generated / (elapsed / 1000.0f);
   200→        Serial.printf("\n\n[%d tokens, %.1f tok/s]\n", generated, tokens_per_sec);
   201→    }
   202→
   203→    free(prompt_tokens);
   204→}

   273→    Serial.println("========================================\n");
