     1→// llm_core.cpp - Int8 Quantized LLM Inference for ESP32-S3
     2→// Based on llama2.c/runq.c - Single-core, adaptive to any model size
     3→
     4→#include "llm_core.h"
     5→#include <math.h>
     6→#include <string.h>
     7→#include <esp_heap_caps.h>  // For heap_caps_aligned_alloc (16-byte aligned SIMD buffers)
     8→
     9→// Global group size (read from model header, typically 32 or 64)
    10→int GS = 64;
    11→
    12→// ============================================================================
    13→// Quantization Functions
    14→// ============================================================================
    15→
    16→void dequantize(QuantizedTensor *qx, float* x, int n) {
    17→    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
    18→        x[i] = qx->q[i] * qx->s[i / GS];
    19→    }
    20→}
    21→
    22→void quantize(QuantizedTensor *qx, float* x, int n) {
    23→    int num_groups = n / GS;
    24→    float Q_MAX = 127.0f;
    25→
    26→    for (int group = 0; group < num_groups; group++) {
    27→        float* gx = x + group * GS;
    28→        int8_t* gq = qx->q + group * GS;
    29→
    30→        // Find max absolute value using SIMD dot product trick:
    31→        // max(|x|) ≈ sqrt(max element of x²) but that's expensive
    32→        // Instead, unroll the loop for better pipelining
    33→        float wmax = 0.0f;
    34→        for (int i = 0; i < GS; i += 4) {
    35→            float v0 = fabsf(gx[i]);
    36→            float v1 = fabsf(gx[i+1]);
    37→            float v2 = fabsf(gx[i+2]);
    38→            float v3 = fabsf(gx[i+3]);
    39→            if (v0 > wmax) wmax = v0;
    40→            if (v1 > wmax) wmax = v1;
    41→            if (v2 > wmax) wmax = v2;
    42→            if (v3 > wmax) wmax = v3;
    43→        }
    44→
    45→        float scale = wmax / Q_MAX;
    46→        qx->s[group] = scale;
    47→
    48→        // Quantize with reciprocal multiply (faster than division)
    49→        float inv_scale = (scale > 1e-10f) ? Q_MAX / wmax : 0.0f;
    50→        for (int i = 0; i < GS; i += 4) {
    51→            gq[i]   = (int8_t)(gx[i]   * inv_scale + 0.5f - (gx[i]   < 0));
    52→            gq[i+1] = (int8_t)(gx[i+1] * inv_scale + 0.5f - (gx[i+1] < 0));
    53→            gq[i+2] = (int8_t)(gx[i+2] * inv_scale + 0.5f - (gx[i+2] < 0));
    54→            gq[i+3] = (int8_t)(gx[i+3] * inv_scale + 0.5f - (gx[i+3] < 0));
    55→        }
    56→    }
    57→}
    58→
    59→// ============================================================================
    60→// Neural Network Operations
    61→// ============================================================================
    62→
    63→void rmsnorm(float* o, float* x, float* weight, int size) {
    64→    // Sum of squares using SIMD dot product
    65→    float ss = 0.0f;
    66→    dsps_dotprod_f32_aes3(x, x, &ss, size);
    67→
    68→    // Normalization factor
    69→    ss = 1.0f / sqrtf(ss / size + 1e-5f);
    70→
    71→    // Scale x by ss, then multiply by weight
    72→    // o[i] = weight[i] * (ss * x[i])
    73→    dsps_mulc_f32_ae32(x, o, size, ss, 1, 1);       // o = x * ss
    74→    dsps_mul_f32_ae32(o, weight, o, size, 1, 1, 1); // o = o * weight
    75→}
    76→
    77→void softmax(float* x, int size) {
    78→    // Find max (no SIMD equivalent that's faster for small arrays)
    79→    float max_val = x[0];
    80→    for (int i = 1; i < size; i++) {
    81→        if (x[i] > max_val) max_val = x[i];
    82→    }
    83→
    84→    // Exp and sum (expf() is the bottleneck, can't SIMD this)
    85→    float sum = 0.0f;
    86→    for (int i = 0; i < size; i++) {
    87→        x[i] = expf(x[i] - max_val);
    88→        sum += x[i];
    89→    }
    90→
    91→    // Vectorized division using SIMD multiply by inverse
    92→    float inv_sum = 1.0f / sum;
    93→    dsps_mulc_f32_ae32(x, x, size, inv_sum, 1, 1);
    94→}
    95→
    96→// PIE SIMD int8 dot product - returns full int32 accumulator
    97→// Processes 16 int8 pairs at a time using ESP32-S3 PIE vector instructions
    98→// Requirements: len must be multiple of 16, both pointers must be 16-byte aligned
    99→static inline int32_t dotprod_s8_simd(const int8_t* a, const int8_t* b, int len) {
   100→    int32_t result;
   101→    int chunks = len >> 4;  // len / 16
   102→
   103→    asm volatile(
   104→        // Clear 40-bit accumulator
   105→        "wur.accx_0 %[zero]\n"
   106→        "wur.accx_1 %[zero]\n"
   107→
   108→        // Process 16 int8 pairs per iteration
   109→        "loopnez %[chunks], 1f\n"
   110→        "ee.vld.128.ip q0, %[a], 16\n"    // Load 16 int8s from a
   111→        "ee.vld.128.ip q1, %[b], 16\n"    // Load 16 int8s from b
   112→        "ee.vmulas.s8.accx q0, q1\n"      // MAC: accx += sum(q0[i] * q1[i])
   113→        "1:\n"
   114→
   115→        // Read low 32 bits of accumulator
   116→        "rur.accx_0 %[result]\n"
   117→
   118→        : [result] "=r" (result), [a] "+r" (a), [b] "+r" (b)
   119→        : [chunks] "r" (chunks), [zero] "r" (0)
   120→        : "memory"
   121→    );
   122→
   123→    return result;
   124→}
   125→
   126→void matmul_q8(float* xout, QuantizedTensor* x, QuantizedTensor* w, int n, int d) {
   127→    for (int i = 0; i < d; i++) {
   128→        float val = 0.0f;
   129→        int in = i * n;
   130→
   131→        // Process each quantization group with SIMD
   132→        for (int j = 0; j <= n - GS; j += GS) {
   133→            // SIMD dot product for this group (GS elements)
   134→            int32_t ival = dotprod_s8_simd(x->q + j, w->q + in + j, GS);
   135→
   136→            // Scale by quantization scales
   137→            val += (float)ival * w->s[(in + j) / GS] * x->s[j / GS];
   138→        }
   139→        xout[i] = val;
   140→    }
   141→}
   142→
   143→// ============================================================================
   144→// Memory Allocation
   145→// ============================================================================
   146→
   147→static bool malloc_run_state(RunState* s, Config* p) {
   148→    int kv_dim = (p->dim * p->n_kv_heads) / p->n_heads;
   149→
   150→    size_t kv_cache_size = (size_t)p->n_layers * p->seq_len * kv_dim * sizeof(float);
   151→    size_t total_needed =
   152→        3 * p->dim * sizeof(float) +
   153→        2 * p->hidden_dim * sizeof(float) +
   154→        p->dim * sizeof(float) +
   155→        p->n_heads * p->seq_len * sizeof(float) +
   156→        p->vocab_size * sizeof(float) +
   157→        2 * kv_cache_size +
   158→        p->dim + p->dim / GS * sizeof(float) +
   159→        p->hidden_dim + p->hidden_dim / GS * sizeof(float);
   160→
   161→    if (total_needed > ESP.getFreePsram()) {
   162→        Serial.println("ERROR: Not enough PSRAM for RunState!");
   163→        return false;
   164→    }
   165→
   166→    s->x = (float*)ps_calloc(p->dim, sizeof(float));
   167→    s->xb = (float*)ps_calloc(p->dim, sizeof(float));
   168→    s->xb2 = (float*)ps_calloc(p->dim, sizeof(float));
   169→    s->hb = (float*)ps_calloc(p->hidden_dim, sizeof(float));
   170→    s->hb2 = (float*)ps_calloc(p->hidden_dim, sizeof(float));
   171→    s->q = (float*)ps_calloc(p->dim, sizeof(float));
   172→    s->att = (float*)ps_calloc(p->n_heads * p->seq_len, sizeof(float));
   173→    s->logits = (float*)ps_calloc(p->vocab_size, sizeof(float));
   174→
   175→    s->key_cache = (float*)ps_calloc(p->n_layers * p->seq_len * kv_dim, sizeof(float));
   176→    s->value_cache = (float*)ps_calloc(p->n_layers * p->seq_len * kv_dim, sizeof(float));
   177→
   178→    // Quantized activation buffers - MUST be 16-byte aligned for PIE SIMD
   179→    s->xq.q = (int8_t*)heap_caps_aligned_alloc(16, p->dim * sizeof(int8_t), MALLOC_CAP_SPIRAM);
   180→    s->xq.s = (float*)ps_calloc(p->dim / GS, sizeof(float));
   181→    s->hq.q = (int8_t*)heap_caps_aligned_alloc(16, p->hidden_dim * sizeof(int8_t), MALLOC_CAP_SPIRAM);
   182→    s->hq.s = (float*)ps_calloc(p->hidden_dim / GS, sizeof(float));
   183→
   184→    if (!s->x || !s->xb || !s->xb2 || !s->hb || !s->hb2 || !s->q ||
   185→        !s->att || !s->logits || !s->key_cache || !s->value_cache ||
   186→        !s->xq.q || !s->xq.s || !s->hq.q || !s->hq.s) {
   187→        Serial.println("ERROR: RunState allocation failed!");
   188→        return false;
   189→    }
   190→
   191→    return true;
   192→}
   193→
   194→static void free_run_state(RunState* s) {
   195→    free(s->x);
   196→    free(s->xb);
   197→    free(s->xb2);
   198→    free(s->hb);
   199→    free(s->hb2);
   200→    free(s->q);
   201→    free(s->att);
   202→    free(s->logits);
   203→    free(s->key_cache);
   204→    free(s->value_cache);
   205→    free(s->xq.q);
   206→    free(s->xq.s);
   207→    free(s->hq.q);
   208→    free(s->hq.s);
   209→}
   210→
   211→// ============================================================================
   212→// Weight Memory Mapping (Q8_0 Format)
   213→// ============================================================================
   214→
   215→static QuantizedTensor* init_quantized_tensors(void** ptr, int n, int size_each) {
   216→    void* p = *ptr;
   217→    QuantizedTensor* res = (QuantizedTensor*)malloc(n * sizeof(QuantizedTensor));
   218→
   219→    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
   220→        res[i].q = (int8_t*)p;
   221→        p = (int8_t*)p + size_each;
   222→        res[i].s = (float*)p;
   223→        p = (float*)p + size_each / GS;
   224→    }
   225→
   226→    *ptr = p;
   227→    return res;
   228→}
   229→
   230→static void memory_map_weights(TransformerWeights* w, Config* p, void* ptr, uint8_t shared_classifier) {
   231→    int head_size = p->dim / p->n_heads;
   232→
   233→    float* fptr = (float*)ptr;
   234→    w->rms_att_weight = fptr;
   235→    fptr += p->n_layers * p->dim;
   236→    w->rms_ffn_weight = fptr;
   237→    fptr += p->n_layers * p->dim;
   238→    w->rms_final_weight = fptr;
   239→    fptr += p->dim;
   240→
   241→    ptr = (void*)fptr;
   242→
   243→    w->q_tokens = init_quantized_tensors(&ptr, 1, p->vocab_size * p->dim);
   244→    w->wq = init_quantized_tensors(&ptr, p->n_layers, p->dim * (p->n_heads * head_size));
   245→    w->wk = init_quantized_tensors(&ptr, p->n_layers, p->dim * (p->n_kv_heads * head_size));
   246→    w->wv = init_quantized_tensors(&ptr, p->n_layers, p->dim * (p->n_kv_heads * head_size));
   247→    w->wo = init_quantized_tensors(&ptr, p->n_layers, (p->n_heads * head_size) * p->dim);
   248→    w->w1 = init_quantized_tensors(&ptr, p->n_layers, p->dim * p->hidden_dim);
   249→    w->w2 = init_quantized_tensors(&ptr, p->n_layers, p->hidden_dim * p->dim);
   250→    w->w3 = init_quantized_tensors(&ptr, p->n_layers, p->dim * p->hidden_dim);
   251→    w->wcls = shared_classifier ? w->q_tokens : init_quantized_tensors(&ptr, 1, p->dim * p->vocab_size);
   252→}
   253→
   254→// ============================================================================
   255→// Transformer Build/Free
   256→// ============================================================================
   257→
   258→bool build_transformer_q8(Transformer* t, const char* checkpoint_path, int max_seq_len) {
   259→    File file = SD.open(checkpoint_path, FILE_READ);
   260→    if (!file) {
   261→        Serial.printf("Failed to open model: %s\n", checkpoint_path);
   262→        return false;
   263→    }
   264→
   265→    uint32_t magic, version;
   266→    file.read((uint8_t*)&magic, 4);
   267→    file.read((uint8_t*)&version, 4);
   268→
   269→    if (magic != 0x616b3432) {
   270→        Serial.printf("Invalid magic: 0x%08X\n", magic);
   271→        file.close();
   272→        return false;
   273→    }
   274→    if (version != 2) {
   275→        Serial.printf("Invalid version: %d\n", version);
   276→        file.close();
   277→        return false;
   278→    }
   279→
   280→    file.read((uint8_t*)&t->config, sizeof(Config));
   281→    file.read(&t->shared_classifier, 1);
   282→    file.read((uint8_t*)&GS, 4);
   283→
   284→    if (max_seq_len > 0 && max_seq_len < t->config.seq_len) {
   285→        t->config.seq_len = max_seq_len;
   286→    }
   287→
   288→    Serial.printf("Model: dim=%d, layers=%d, vocab=%d, seq=%d\n",
   289→                  t->config.dim, t->config.n_layers,
   290→                  t->config.vocab_size, t->config.seq_len);
   291→
   292→    t->file_size = file.size();
   293→    // MUST be 16-byte aligned for PIE SIMD weight access
   294→    t->raw_data = (uint8_t*)heap_caps_aligned_alloc(16, t->file_size, MALLOC_CAP_SPIRAM);
   295→    if (!t->raw_data) {
   296→        Serial.println("PSRAM allocation failed!");
   297→        file.close();
   298→        return false;
   299→    }
   300→
   301→    file.seek(0);
   302→    size_t bytes_read = file.read(t->raw_data, t->file_size);
   303→    file.close();
   304→
   305→    if (bytes_read != t->file_size) {
   306→        free(t->raw_data);
   307→        return false;
   308→    }
   309→
   310→    memory_map_weights(&t->weights, &t->config, t->raw_data + 256, t->shared_classifier);
   311→
   312→    int emb_size = t->config.vocab_size * t->config.dim;
   313→    t->weights.token_embedding_table = (float*)ps_malloc(emb_size * sizeof(float));
   314→    if (!t->weights.token_embedding_table) {
   315→        Serial.println("Embedding allocation failed!");
   316→        free(t->raw_data);
   317→        return false;
   318→    }
   319→
   320→    dequantize(t->weights.q_tokens, t->weights.token_embedding_table, emb_size);
   321→
   322→    if (!malloc_run_state(&t->state, &t->config)) {
   323→        free(t->weights.token_embedding_table);
   324→        free(t->raw_data);
   325→        return false;
   326→    }
   327→
   328→    // Initialize RoPE cache
   329→    init_rope_cache(t);
   330→
   331→    Serial.println("Model ready!");
   332→    return true;
   333→}
   334→
   335→void init_rope_cache(Transformer* t) {
   336→    int head_size = t->config.dim / t->config.n_heads;
   337→    int half_head = head_size / 2;
   338→    int cache_size = t->config.seq_len * half_head;
   339→
   340→    t->rope_cos = (float*)ps_malloc(cache_size * sizeof(float));
   341→    t->rope_sin = (float*)ps_malloc(cache_size * sizeof(float));
   342→
   343→    if (!t->rope_cos || !t->rope_sin) {
   344→        Serial.println("Warning: RoPE cache allocation failed, using runtime trig");
   345→        return;
   346→    }
   347→
   348→    // Precompute sin/cos for all positions and head dimensions
   349→    for (int pos = 0; pos < t->config.seq_len; pos++) {
   350→        for (int i = 0; i < half_head; i++) {
   351→            float freq = 1.0f / powf(10000.0f, (2.0f * i) / head_size);
   352→            float val = pos * freq;
   353→            t->rope_cos[pos * half_head + i] = cosf(val);
   354→            t->rope_sin[pos * half_head + i] = sinf(val);
   355→        }
   356→    }
   357→
   358→    Serial.printf("RoPE cache: %d KB\n", (cache_size * 2 * sizeof(float)) / 1024);
   359→}
   360→
   361→void free_transformer(Transformer* t) {
   362→    if (t->raw_data) {
   363→        free(t->raw_data);
   364→        t->raw_data = nullptr;
   365→    }
   366→    if (t->weights.token_embedding_table) {
   367→        free(t->weights.token_embedding_table);
   368→        t->weights.token_embedding_table = nullptr;
   369→    }
   370→    if (t->rope_cos) {
   371→        free(t->rope_cos);
   372→        t->rope_cos = nullptr;
   373→    }
   374→    if (t->rope_sin) {
   375→        free(t->rope_sin);
   376→        t->rope_sin = nullptr;
   377→    }
   378→
   379→    free(t->weights.q_tokens);
   380→    free(t->weights.wq);
   381→    free(t->weights.wk);
   382→    free(t->weights.wv);
   383→    free(t->weights.wo);
   384→    free(t->weights.w1);
   385→    free(t->weights.w2);
   386→    free(t->weights.w3);
   387→    if (!t->shared_classifier) {
   388→        free(t->weights.wcls);
   389→    }
   390→
   391→    free_run_state(&t->state);
   392→}
   393→
   394→// ============================================================================
   395→// Forward Pass
   396→// ============================================================================
   397→
   398→float* forward(Transformer* transformer, int token, int pos) {
   399→    Config* p = &transformer->config;
   400→    TransformerWeights* w = &transformer->weights;
   401→    RunState* s = &transformer->state;
   402→
   403→    int dim = p->dim;
   404→    int kv_dim = (dim * p->n_kv_heads) / p->n_heads;
   405→    int kv_mul = p->n_heads / p->n_kv_heads;
   406→    int hidden_dim = p->hidden_dim;
   407→    int head_size = dim / p->n_heads;
   408→
   409→    if (token < 0 || token >= p->vocab_size) {
   410→        return nullptr;
   411→    }
   412→
   413→    // Copy token embedding
   414→    float* content_row = w->token_embedding_table + token * dim;
   415→    memcpy(s->x, content_row, dim * sizeof(float));
   416→
   417→    // Forward through all layers
   418→    for (int l = 0; l < p->n_layers; l++) {
   419→        rmsnorm(s->xb, s->x, w->rms_att_weight + l * dim, dim);
   420→
   421→        int loff = l * p->seq_len * kv_dim;
   422→        s->k = s->key_cache + loff + pos * kv_dim;
   423→        s->v = s->value_cache + loff + pos * kv_dim;
   424→
   425→        quantize(&s->xq, s->xb, dim);
   426→        matmul_q8(s->q, &s->xq, &w->wq[l], dim, dim);
   427→        matmul_q8(s->k, &s->xq, &w->wk[l], dim, kv_dim);
   428→        matmul_q8(s->v, &s->xq, &w->wv[l], dim, kv_dim);
   429→
   430→        // RoPE with cached sin/cos lookup (eliminates runtime trig)
   431→        int half_head = head_size / 2;
   432→        float* cos_ptr = transformer->rope_cos + pos * half_head;
   433→        float* sin_ptr = transformer->rope_sin + pos * half_head;
   434→
   435→        for (int i = 0; i < dim; i += 2) {
   436→            int idx = (i / 2) % half_head;
   437→            float fcr = cos_ptr[idx];
   438→            float fci = sin_ptr[idx];
   439→            int rotn = i < kv_dim ? 2 : 1;
   440→            for (int v = 0; v < rotn; v++) {
   441→                float* vec = v == 0 ? s->q : s->k;
   442→                float v0 = vec[i];
   443→                float v1 = vec[i + 1];
   444→                vec[i] = v0 * fcr - v1 * fci;
   445→                vec[i + 1] = v0 * fci + v1 * fcr;
   446→            }
   447→        }
   448→
   449→        // Multi-head attention with SIMD
   450→        float scale = 1.0f / sqrtf(head_size);
   451→        for (int h = 0; h < p->n_heads; h++) {
   452→            float* q = s->q + h * head_size;
   453→            float* att = s->att + h * p->seq_len;
   454→
   455→            // Attention scoring with SIMD dot product
   456→            for (int t = 0; t <= pos; t++) {
   457→                float* k = s->key_cache + loff + t * kv_dim + (h / kv_mul) * head_size;
   458→                float score = 0.0f;
   459→                dsps_dotprod_f32_aes3(q, k, &score, head_size);
   460→                att[t] = score * scale;
   461→            }
   462→
   463→            softmax(att, pos + 1);
   464→
   465→            // Attention aggregation with SIMD
   466→            float* xb = s->xb + h * head_size;
   467→            memset(xb, 0, head_size * sizeof(float));
   468→            for (int t = 0; t <= pos; t++) {
   469→                float* v = s->value_cache + loff + t * kv_dim + (h / kv_mul) * head_size;
   470→                float a = att[t];
   471→                // xb += a * v using SIMD: temp = v * a, xb += temp
   472→                dsps_mulc_f32_ae32(v, s->xb2, head_size, a, 1, 1);
   473→                dsps_add_f32_ae32(xb, s->xb2, xb, head_size, 1, 1, 1);
   474→            }
   475→        }
   476→
   477→        quantize(&s->xq, s->xb, dim);
   478→        matmul_q8(s->xb2, &s->xq, &w->wo[l], dim, dim);
   479→
   480→        // Residual connection with SIMD
   481→        dsps_add_f32_ae32(s->x, s->xb2, s->x, dim, 1, 1, 1);
   482→
   483→        rmsnorm(s->xb, s->x, w->rms_ffn_weight + l * dim, dim);
   484→
   485→        quantize(&s->xq, s->xb, dim);
   486→        matmul_q8(s->hb, &s->xq, &w->w1[l], dim, hidden_dim);
   487→        matmul_q8(s->hb2, &s->xq, &w->w3[l], dim, hidden_dim);
   488→
   489→        // SwiGLU with fast sigmoid approximation
   490→        // sigmoid(x) ≈ 0.5 + 0.5 * tanh(x * 0.5) ≈ x / (1 + |x|) for speed
   491→        // But for SiLU we need decent accuracy, use: 1/(1+exp(-x)) ≈ fast approx
   492→        for (int i = 0; i < hidden_dim; i += 4) {
   493→            // Unrolled for better pipelining
   494→            float v0 = s->hb[i], v1 = s->hb[i+1], v2 = s->hb[i+2], v3 = s->hb[i+3];
   495→            // SiLU: x * sigmoid(x)
   496→            v0 *= 1.0f / (1.0f + expf(-v0));
   497→            v1 *= 1.0f / (1.0f + expf(-v1));
   498→            v2 *= 1.0f / (1.0f + expf(-v2));
   499→            v3 *= 1.0f / (1.0f + expf(-v3));
   500→            // Gate multiply
   501→            s->hb[i]   = v0 * s->hb2[i];
   502→            s->hb[i+1] = v1 * s->hb2[i+1];
   503→            s->hb[i+2] = v2 * s->hb2[i+2];
   504→            s->hb[i+3] = v3 * s->hb2[i+3];
   505→        }
   506→
   507→        quantize(&s->hq, s->hb, hidden_dim);
   508→        matmul_q8(s->xb, &s->hq, &w->w2[l], hidden_dim, dim);
   509→
   510→        // Residual connection with SIMD
   511→        dsps_add_f32_ae32(s->x, s->xb, s->x, dim, 1, 1, 1);
   512→    }
   513→
   514→    rmsnorm(s->x, s->x, w->rms_final_weight, dim);
   515→
   516→    quantize(&s->xq, s->x, dim);
   517→    matmul_q8(s->logits, &s->xq, w->wcls, dim, p->vocab_size);
   518→
   519→    return s->logits;
   520→}
   521→

    21→    _y = y;
    22→    _widthLimit = widthLimit;
    23→    _heightLimit = heightLimit;
    24→    _inputindex = 0;
    25→
    26→    if (!_read_buf) {
    27→      _read_buf = (uint8_t *)malloc(READ_BUFFER_SIZE);
    28→    }
    29→    return _read_buf != nullptr;
    30→  }
    31→
    32→  // Read next JPEG frame from MJPEG stream (searches for FF D8/FF D9 markers)
    33→  bool readMjpegBuf() {
    34→    if (_inputindex == 0) {
    35→      _buf_read = _input->readBytes(_read_buf, READ_BUFFER_SIZE);
    36→      _inputindex += _buf_read;
    37→    }
    38→    _mjpeg_buf_offset = 0;
    39→    int i = 0;
    40→    bool found_FFD8 = false;
    41→
    42→    // Search for JPEG Start of Image (FF D8)
    43→    while ((_buf_read > 0) && (!found_FFD8)) {
    44→      i = 0;
    45→      while ((i < _buf_read) && (!found_FFD8)) {
    46→        if ((_read_buf[i] == 0xFF) && (_read_buf[i + 1] == 0xD8)) {
    47→          found_FFD8 = true;
    48→        }
    49→        ++i;
    50→      }
    51→      if (found_FFD8) {
    52→        --i;
    53→      } else {
    54→        _buf_read = _input->readBytes(_read_buf, READ_BUFFER_SIZE);
    55→      }
    56→    }
    57→
    58→    uint8_t *_p = _read_buf + i;
    59→    _buf_read -= i;
    60→    bool found_FFD9 = false;
    61→
    62→    // Copy JPEG data and search for End of Image (FF D9)
    63→    if (_buf_read > 0) {
    64→      i = 3;
    65→      while ((_buf_read > 0) && (!found_FFD9)) {
    66→        if ((_mjpeg_buf_offset > 0) && (_mjpeg_buf[_mjpeg_buf_offset - 1] == 0xFF) && (_p[0] == 0xD9)) {
    67→          found_FFD9 = true;
    68→        } else {
    69→          while ((i < _buf_read) && (!found_FFD9)) {
    70→            if ((_p[i] == 0xFF) && (_p[i + 1] == 0xD9)) {
    71→              found_FFD9 = true;
    72→              ++i;
    73→            }
    74→            ++i;
    75→          }
    76→        }
    77→
    78→        memcpy(_mjpeg_buf + _mjpeg_buf_offset, _p, i);
    79→        _mjpeg_buf_offset += i;
    80→        size_t o = _buf_read - i;
    81→
    82→        if (o > 0) {
    83→          memcpy(_read_buf, _p + i, o);
    84→          _buf_read = _input->readBytes(_read_buf + o, READ_BUFFER_SIZE - o);
    85→          _p = _read_buf;
    86→          _inputindex += _buf_read;
    87→          _buf_read += o;
    88→        } else {
    89→          _buf_read = _input->readBytes(_read_buf, READ_BUFFER_SIZE);
    90→          _p = _read_buf;
    91→          _inputindex += _buf_read;
    92→        }
    93→        i = 0;
    94→      }
    95→      return found_FFD9;
    96→    }
    97→    return false;
    98→  }
    99→
   100→  // Decode and draw current JPEG frame
   101→  bool drawJpg() {
   102→    _remain = _mjpeg_buf_offset;
   103→
   104→    if (_jpeg.openRAM(_mjpeg_buf, _remain, _pfnDraw) != 1) return false;
   105→
   106→    if (_scale == -1) {
   107→      // Calculate scale to fit screen
   108→      int iMaxMCUs;
   109→      int w = _jpeg.getWidth();
   110→      int h = _jpeg.getHeight();
   111→      float ratio = (float)h / _heightLimit;
   112→
   113→      if (ratio <= 1) {
   114→        _scale = 0;
   115→        iMaxMCUs = _widthLimit / 16;
   116→      } else if (ratio <= 2) {
   117→        _scale = JPEG_SCALE_HALF;
   118→        iMaxMCUs = _widthLimit / 8;
   119→        w /= 2;
   120→        h /= 2;
   121→      } else if (ratio <= 4) {
   122→        _scale = JPEG_SCALE_QUARTER;
   123→        iMaxMCUs = _widthLimit / 4;
   124→        w /= 4;
   125→        h /= 4;
   126→      } else {
   127→        _scale = JPEG_SCALE_EIGHTH;
   128→        iMaxMCUs = _widthLimit / 2;
   129→        w /= 8;
   130→        h /= 8;
   131→      }
   132→
   133→      _jpeg.setMaxOutputSize(iMaxMCUs);
   134→      _x = (w > _widthLimit) ? 0 : ((_widthLimit - w) / 2);
   135→      _y = (_heightLimit - h) / 2;
   136→    }
   137→
   138→    if (_useBigEndian) {
   139→      _jpeg.setPixelType(RGB565_BIG_ENDIAN);
   140→    }
   141→
   142→    if (_jpeg.decode(_x, _y, _scale) != 1) {
   143→      _jpeg.close();
   144→      return false;
   145→    }
   146→
   147→    _jpeg.close();
   148→    return true;
   149→  }
   150→
   151→  // Reset decoder state for looping
   152→  void reset() {
   153→    _inputindex = 0;
   154→    _buf_read = 0;
   155→    _mjpeg_buf_offset = 0;
   156→  }
   157→
   158→private:
   159→  Stream *_input;
   160→  uint8_t *_mjpeg_buf;
   161→  JPEG_DRAW_CALLBACK *_pfnDraw;
   162→  bool _useBigEndian;
   163→  int _x, _y, _widthLimit, _heightLimit;
   164→  uint8_t *_read_buf = nullptr;
   165→  int32_t _mjpeg_buf_offset = 0;
   166→  JPEGDEC _jpeg;
   167→  int _scale = -1;
   168→  int32_t _inputindex = 0;
   169→  int32_t _buf_read;
   170→  int32_t _remain = 0;
   171→};

## SAM (Software Automatic Mouth) TTS for ESP32

SAM is a very small Text-To-Speech (TTS) program written in C that runs on most popular platforms. Phil Schatzmann created a project with the intention to provide SAM as an Arduino Library with a simple API that supports different output alternatives.

### ESP8266SAM Library
The ESP8266SAM library can be utilized with the ESP8266Audio library to have your ESP speak via a DAC or a direct-drive speaker. No web services are required - everything from text parsing to speech generation is done directly on the ESP.(no content)The SAM software is a reverse-engineered version of software published more than 34 years ago by "Don't ask Software". The company no longer exists and attempts to contact the original authors failed, so SAM can be best described as Abandonware.

### Other TTS Options for ESP32

**ESP32Talkie:**
There's an Arduino "Talkie" text-to-speech sketch (LPC-10 codec) converted to ESP32 Arduino-IDE available at https://github.com/bobh/ESP32Talkie. It stores speech in much smaller files than .wav format and has a phrase library.(no content)It emulates the Texas Instruments TMS5220 chip which was used in their Speak and Spell product from the 1980's - famous in the Spielberg movie "ET the Extra-Terrestrial."

**PicoTTS for ESP32-S3:**
One user reported getting PicoTTS to work on an ESP32-S3 that doesn't have a DSP on board by rewriting the initialization component using the I2S module.(no content)The PicoTTS engine was ported to an ESP-IDF component for the ESP-BOX. While the voice is nowhere near the quality of OpenAI's, it's still remarkably good considering the limited resources. You get a choice between English (UK/US), German, French, Italian and Spanish voices.

**Espressif's Official TTS:**
Espressif provides an official esp-tts library with Chinese voice synthesis support for ESP32-S3.

### Key Libraries to Check:
1. **ESP8266SAM** - https://github.com/earlephilhower/ESP8266SAM (works with ESP8266Audio)
2. **Phil Schatzmann's SAM Arduino Library** - Provides SAM with Arduino-compatible API
3. **ESP32Talkie** - https://github.com/bobh/ESP32Talkie
4. **PicoTTS** - ESP-IDF component for more natural-sounding speech

## Key Findings

### QMI8658 IMU with ESP32-S3

The QMI8658 is a six-axis IMU that can be interfaced via I2C, allowing you to read accelerometer and gyroscope data for motion tracking and gesture recognition. Several Waveshare ESP32-S3 development boards feature this sensor:

- The ESP32-S3-AMOLED-1.91 is a development board by Waveshare that supports 2.4GHz WiFi and BLE 5, with onboard RTC, IMU (QMI8658) and a 1.91-inch AMOLED screen.

- The ESP32-S3-Matrix has an onboard QMI8658 6-axis IMU (3-axis accelerometer and 3-axis gyroscope) for tilt angle and speed measurement.

### Deep Sleep Wake-up Implementation

ESP32 allows deep-sleep wakeup from both GPIO interrupts and timer based interrupt, and it also provides a function that tells you if the last wakeup was from a GPIO or a timer.(no content)For deep sleep wake-up from an accelerometer, RTC GPIO is required. This is an important consideration when connecting the IMU's interrupt pin.

### Accelerometer Wake-up Approach

A common approach is to put the ESP32 in deep sleep and have the accelerometer (like MPU6050) wake it when it detects movement. The same concept applies to the QMI8658.

To implement this, you need to enable GPIO wakeup using functions like `gpio_wakeup_enable()` and `esp_sleep_enable_gpio_wakeup()`, configuring the appropriate interrupt level (high or low) based on your accelerometer's interrupt output.

### QMI8658 Sensor Initialization

The QMI8658 device can be initialized to read accelerometer data, gyroscope data, and temperature data in a continuous loop.(no content)Key functionality includes sensor initialization (setting up the QMI8658C to read acceleration and gyroscope data) and step detection logic using acceleration data through a threshold-based algorithm.

### Important Notes

- You may need to update the QMI8658c.cpp and QMI8658c.h files from the ALICHOUCHENE/Qmi8658c GitHub repository to ensure compatibility with ESP32.

- The power button on some boards can be configured for various power management routines, including low-power mode activation or conditional wake-ups via external triggers.

To implement QMI8658 wake-up from deep sleep on ESP32-S3, you would typically:
1. Configure the QMI8658's motion detection/interrupt feature
2. Connect the IMU's INT pin to an RTC-capable GPIO on the ESP32-S3
3. Use `esp_sleep_enable_ext0_wakeup()` or `esp_sleep_enable_ext1_wakeup()` to configure external wake-up
4. Enter deep sleep with `esp_deep_sleep_start()`

    63→## 📝 Recording Real Voices
    64→
    65→### Requirements

   152→## 🛠️ Tools & Scripts
   153→
   154→### Check Audio Quality
   155→```python
   156→import librosa
   157→import numpy as np
   158→
   159→audio, sr = librosa.load('recording.wav')
   160→
   161→# RMS level (should be 0.1-0.5)
   162→rms = np.sqrt(np.mean(audio**2))
   163→print(f"RMS: {rms:.3f}")
   164→
   165→# Clipping (should be 0)
   166→clipped = np.sum(np.abs(audio) > 0.99)
   167→print(f"Clipped samples: {clipped}")
   168→
   169→# Duration
   170→duration = len(audio) / sr
   171→print(f"Duration: {duration:.2f} sec")
   172→```
   173→
   174→### Batch Convert Audio
   175→```bash
   176→# Convert all M4A to WAV
   177→for f in *.m4a; do
   178→    ffmpeg -i "$f" -ar 16000 -ac 1 "${f%.m4a}.wav"
   179→done
   180→
   181→# Normalize volume
   182→for f in *.wav; do
   183→    ffmpeg -i "$f" -filter:a "volume=1.5" -ar 16000 "norm_$f"
   184→done
   185→```
   186→
   187→### Generate Labels CSV
   188→```python
   189→import os
   190→import csv
   191→
   192→# Mapping of keywords to query indices
   193→query_map = {
   194→    'schedule': 0,
   195→    'booth': 1,
   196→    'room': 2,
   197→    'contact': 3,
   198→    'note': 4,
   199→    'map': 5,
   200→    'message': 6,
   201→    'profile': 7,
   202→    'session': 8,
   203→    'connect': 9
   204→}
   205→
   206→# Auto-generate labels from filenames
   207→recordings_dir = 'real_recordings/'
   208→labels = []
   209→
   210→for filename in os.listdir(recordings_dir):
   211→    if not filename.endswith('.wav'):
   212→        continue
   213→
   214→    # Extract query from filename (e.g., "alice_schedule.wav")
   215→    for keyword, idx in query_map.items():
   216→        if keyword in filename.lower():
   217→            labels.append({
   218→                'filename': filename,
   219→                'query_idx': idx,
   220→                'text': f'Automatically detected: {keyword}'
   221→            })
   222→            break
   223→
   224→# Save to CSV
   225→with open('labels.csv', 'w', newline='') as f:
   226→    writer = csv.DictWriter(f, fieldnames=['filename', 'query_idx', 'text'])
   227→    writer.writeheader()
   228→    writer.writerows(labels)
   229→
   230→print(f"Generated labels for {len(labels)} recordings")
   231→```

   300→## 🐛 Troubleshooting
   301→
   302→**Problem:** Low accuracy after fine-tuning
   303→- ✅ Check audio quality (RMS, clipping)
   304→- ✅ Use lower learning rate (1e-5 instead of 1e-4)
   305→- ✅ Mix with XTTS data (--mix-with-xtts flag)
   306→
   307→**Problem:** Model forgot XTTS knowledge
   308→- ✅ Use very low learning rate (1e-5 or 1e-6)
   309→- ✅ Train fewer epochs (50 instead of 100)
   310→- ✅ Always mix real + XTTS data
   311→
   312→**Problem:** Audio files have errors
   313→- ✅ Convert to 16kHz mono: `ffmpeg -i input.wav -ar 16000 -ac 1 output.wav`
   314→- ✅ Check duration: Minimum 1 second, recommended 2-5 seconds
   315→- ✅ Normalize volume: Should not clip (max < 0.99)

# OAISYS25 Badge Unified Firmware Implementation Plan

## Executive Summary

This plan details the integration of 6 working ESP32-S3 prototypes into a unified badge application with:
- State machine driven operation
- Memory-managed ML model swapping (only one model loaded at a time)
- Robotic TTS using ESP8266SAM
- Deep sleep with IMU-based shake wake
- WiFi connectivity for model updates
- FastAPI + Redis backend for transcription and corrections

---

## 1. Firmware Architecture

### 1.1 State Machine Design

\```
                    ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
                    │                                                         │
                    ▼                                                         │
    ┌──────────┐   5min idle    ┌────────────┐   shake detected              │
    │   BOOT   │ ──────────────►│ DEEP_SLEEP │ ──────────────────────────────┤
    └────┬─────┘                └────────────┘                               │
         │                                                                    │
         ▼                                                                    │
    ┌──────────┐   button/wake_word    ┌───────────┐                        │
    │LOGO_LOOP │ ────────────────────► │ RECORDING │                        │
    └──────────┘                       └─────┬─────┘                        │
         ▲                                   │ 3-5 sec                      │
         │                                   ▼                              │
         │                            ┌───────────┐                         │
         │                            │PROCESSING │ (YAMNet → embedding)    │
         │                            └─────┬─────┘                         │
         │                                  │                               │
         │               ┌──────────────────┴──────────────────┐            │
         │               ▼                                     ▼            │
         │        score >= 0.7                          score < 0.7        │
         │               │                                     │            │
         │               ▼                                     ▼            │
         │        ┌──────────────┐                     ┌────────────┐       │
         │        │LLM_INFERENCE │                     │ TTS_SORRY  │       │
         │        └──────┬───────┘                     └──────┬─────┘       │
         │               │                                    │             │
         │               ▼                                    │             │
         │        ┌──────────────┐                            │             │
         │        │DISPLAY_RESP  │ (text overlay)             │             │
         │        └──────┬───────┘                            │             │
         │               │                                    │             │
         │               ▼                                    │             │
         │        ┌──────────────┐                     ┌────────────┐       │
         │        │  TTS_OUTPUT  │                     │ STASH_DATA │       │
         │        └──────┬───────┘                     └──────┬─────┘       │
         │               │                                    │             │
         └───────────────┴────────────────────────────────────┘             │
                                                                            │
\```

### 1.2 State Enum Definition

\```cpp
enum class BadgeState : uint8_t {
    BOOT,
    LOGO_LOOP,
    DEEP_SLEEP,
    RECORDING,
    PROCESSING,
    LLM_INFERENCE,
    DISPLAY_RESPONSE,
    TTS_OUTPUT,
    TTS_SORRY,
    STASH_DATA,
    WIFI_SYNC       // Background state for model updates
};
\```

### 1.3 Module Interface Pattern

Each module follows `begin()/end()` pattern for memory management:

\```cpp
// Module interface template
class ModuleBase {
public:
    virtual bool begin() = 0;      // Allocate PSRAM, load model
    virtual void end() = 0;        // Free PSRAM, unload model
    virtual bool isLoaded() const = 0;
    virtual size_t memoryUsage() const = 0;
};

// Concrete modules:
class WakeWordModule : public ModuleBase { ... };   // ~700KB
class YamNetModule : public ModuleBase { ... };     // ~600KB
class LLMModule : public ModuleBase { ... };        // ~5.5MB
class VideoModule : public ModuleBase { ... };      // ~2-3MB (can coexist with wake word)
class TTSModule : public ModuleBase { ... };        // ~50KB (SAM is tiny)
\```

### 1.4 Memory Management Strategy

**PSRAM Budget: ~8MB available**

| Phase | Modules Loaded | Est. PSRAM Usage |
|-------|---------------|------------------|
| LOGO_LOOP | Video + WakeWord | ~3.5MB |
| RECORDING | Audio buffers only | ~100KB |
| PROCESSING | YAMNet | ~600KB |
| LLM_INFERENCE | LLM | ~5.5MB |
| TTS_OUTPUT | SAM | ~50KB |

**Memory Pool Design:**

\```cpp
class MemoryPool {
public:
    // Pre-allocate 6MB PSRAM pool at boot
    bool init(size_t pool_size = 6 * 1024 * 1024);
    
    // Allocate from pool (16-byte aligned for SIMD)
    void* allocate(size_t size);
    
    // Free entire pool (used during model swap)
    void reset();
    
    // Stats
    size_t available() const;
    size_t used() const;
    
private:
    uint8_t* pool_;
    size_t pool_size_;
    size_t offset_;
};
\```

### 1.5 FreeRTOS Task Structure

\```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  Core 0                          │  Core 1                 │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  main_task (priority 5)          │  inference_task (pri 4) │
│  - State machine                 │  - TFLite inference     │
│  - Button handling               │  - LLM forward pass     │
│  - Display updates               │                         │
│                                  │                         │
│  audio_task (priority 6)         │  wifi_task (priority 2) │
│  - I2S mic capture               │  - Background sync      │
│  - Wake word streaming           │  - Model downloads      │
│  - Recording to buffer           │                         │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
\```

## 3. Implementation Phases

### Phase 1: Core Integration (Video + Button + Wake Word)

**Duration: 3-4 days**

**Goal:** Video loop with wake word detection running concurrently

**Tasks:**

### Phase 2: ML Pipeline (Recording -> Embedding -> Similarity)

**Duration: 4-5 days**

**Goal:** Record audio, extract YAMNet embedding, match against dataset

**Tasks:**
1. Implement `AudioModule` with recording mode
2. Port `MelSpectrogram` from `04_yamnet_audio_embedding`
3. Port `YamNetModule` with begin/end pattern
4. Implement `ProjectionLayer` using ESP-DSP SIMD:
   \```cpp
   // projection_layer.cpp
   void project_1024_to_256(float* input, float* output, float* weights) {
       // W is 256x1024 matrix
       // output[i] = dot(W[i], input) for i in 0..255
       for (int i = 0; i < 256; i++) {
           float* row = weights + i * 1024;
           dsps_dotprod_f32_aes3(row, input, &output[i], 1024);
       }
   }
   \```
5. Implement `EmbeddingSimilarity`:
   \```cpp
   // Cosine similarity using SIMD
   float cosine_similarity(float* a, float* b, int dim) {
       float dot, norm_a, norm_b;
       dsps_dotprod_f32_aes3(a, b, &dot, dim);
       dsps_dotprod_f32_aes3(a, a, &norm_a, dim);
       dsps_dotprod_f32_aes3(b, b, &norm_b, dim);
       return dot / (sqrtf(norm_a) * sqrtf(norm_b));
   }
   \```
6. Create dataset loader for `query_embeddings.bin`

**State Transitions:**
\```
LOGO_LOOP --[wake_word]--> RECORDING
    ↓ (unload wake word)
    ↓ (record 3-5 sec)
RECORDING --[timeout]--> PROCESSING
    ↓ (unload video buffer)
    ↓ (load YAMNet)
PROCESSING --[embedding_ready]--> [similarity check]
    ↓ score >= 0.7: LLM_INFERENCE
    ↓ score < 0.7:  TTS_SORRY
\```

**Memory Swap Sequence:**
\```cpp
void transitionToProcessing() {

    videoModule.end();   // Free ~2.5MB

    yamnet.begin();      // Allocate ~600KB

}
\```

**QMI8658 Motion Detection:**
\```cpp
// Configure any-motion interrupt
void configureMotionWake() {
    // Set motion threshold (shake detection)
    IMU.writeRegister(QMI8658_WOM_THRESHOLD, 0x10);  // ~0.5g
    
    // Enable any-motion interrupt on INT1
    IMU.writeRegister(QMI8658_CTRL1, 0x01);
}
\```

**Deep Sleep Entry:**
\```cpp
void enterDeepSleep() {
    // Turn off display
    digitalWrite(LCD_BL, LOW);
    display->displayOff();
    
    // Unload all modules
    memoryPool.reset();
    
    // Configure wakeup from QMI8658 INT
    esp_sleep_enable_ext0_wakeup(GPIO_NUM_46, 1);  // Wake on HIGH
    
    // Enter deep sleep
    esp_deep_sleep_start();
}
\```

## 4. Critical Implementation Details

### 4.1 Text Overlay on Video Loop

**Challenge:** Drawing text over MJPEG without blocking video playback

**Solution:** Double-buffer approach
\```cpp
class OverlayVideoPlayer {
    void playFrame() {
        // 1. Decode JPEG frame to framebuffer
        decoder.readMjpegBuf();
        decoder.drawJpg();  // Draws to display
        
        // 2. If overlay active, draw text directly
        if (overlay_text_) {
            // Draw on display after JPEG (quick operation)
            drawOverlay();
        }
    }
    
    void drawOverlay() {
        // Semi-transparent background bar (bottom 1/3)
        for (int y = 200; y < 320; y++) {
            for (int x = 0; x < 240; x++) {
                // Blend with existing pixel
                uint16_t pixel = display->readPixel(x, y);
                uint16_t blended = blendColor(pixel, 0x0000, 128);
                display->drawPixel(x, y, blended);
            }
        }
        
        // Draw text
        display->setTextColor(WHITE);
        display->setCursor(10, 210);
        display->print(overlay_text_);
    }
};
\```

**Optimization:** Pre-render text to off-screen buffer, then blit:
\```cpp
// Create overlay buffer in PSRAM
uint16_t* overlay_buffer = (uint16_t*)ps_malloc(240 * 120 * 2);

// Pre-render text
void updateOverlayText(const char* text) {
    // Clear buffer
    memset(overlay_buffer, 0, 240 * 120 * 2);
    
    // Draw text to buffer
    gfx->drawText(overlay_buffer, 240, 120, text);
}

// Blend into framebuffer after each video frame
void blitOverlay() {
    display->draw16bitRGBBitmap(0, 200, overlay_buffer, 240, 120);
}
\```

### 4.2 Wake Word to Recording Transition

**Challenge:** Seamlessly switch from wake word listening to recording

**Solution:** Pre-buffer approach
\```cpp
class AudioPipeline {
    // Ring buffer holding last 1 second of audio
    int16_t pre_buffer_[16000];
    int pre_buffer_pos_ = 0;
    
    // Recording buffer
    int16_t* record_buffer_;
    int record_pos_ = 0;
    
    void onWakeWordDetected() {
        // 1. Allocate recording buffer
        record_buffer_ = (int16_t*)ps_malloc(RECORD_SAMPLES * 2);
        
        // 2. Copy pre-buffer (last 1 sec before wake word)
        int start = (pre_buffer_pos_ + 1) % 16000;
        for (int i = 0; i < 16000; i++) {
            record_buffer_[i] = pre_buffer_[(start + i) % 16000];
        }
        record_pos_ = 16000;
        
        // 3. Continue recording for 3-4 more seconds
        recording_mode_ = true;
    }
};
\```

### 4.3 Memory Pool Design

\```cpp
// memory_pool.h
class MemoryPool {
public:
    static constexpr size_t POOL_SIZE = 6 * 1024 * 1024;  // 6MB
    static constexpr size_t ALIGNMENT = 16;  // For SIMD
    
    bool init() {
        pool_ = (uint8_t*)heap_caps_aligned_alloc(
            ALIGNMENT, 
            POOL_SIZE, 
            MALLOC_CAP_SPIRAM
        );
        return pool_ != nullptr;
    }
    
    void* allocate(size_t size) {
        // Align size to 16 bytes
        size = (size + ALIGNMENT - 1) & ~(ALIGNMENT - 1);
        
        if (offset_ + size > POOL_SIZE) {
            Serial.printf("Pool exhausted! Requested %u, available %u\n",
                          size, POOL_SIZE - offset_);
            return nullptr;
        }
        
        void* ptr = pool_ + offset_;
        offset_ += size;
        return ptr;
    }
    
    void reset() {
        offset_ = 0;
        memset(pool_, 0, POOL_SIZE);  // Clear for safety
    }
    
    size_t available() const { return POOL_SIZE - offset_; }
    size_t used() const { return offset_; }
    
private:
    uint8_t* pool_ = nullptr;
    size_t offset_ = 0;
};

// Global instance
extern MemoryPool g_memoryPool;
\```

### 4.4 Robotic TTS Approach

**Recommended: ESP8266SAM library**

SAM (Software Automatic Mouth) provides:
- Tiny footprint (~50KB)
- Configurable voice parameters
- Phoneme-based synthesis (robotic quality)
- No external dependencies

\```cpp
#include <ESP8266SAM.h>
#include <AudioOutputI2S.h>

class RoboticTTS {
public:
    bool begin() {
        audio_out_ = new AudioOutputI2S();
        audio_out_->SetPinout(SPK_BCK_PIN, SPK_WS_PIN, SPK_DOUT_PIN);
        audio_out_->SetGain(1.5);
        
        sam_ = new SAM();
        sam_->SetVoice(SAM_VOICE_ELF);  // Robotic preset
        sam_->SetSpeed(72);
        sam_->SetPitch(64);
        
        return true;
    }
    
    void speak(const char* text) {
        // Convert to uppercase (SAM works better)
        char upper[256];
        for (int i = 0; text[i] && i < 255; i++) {
            upper[i] = toupper(text[i]);
        }
        upper[strlen(text)] = 0;
        
        // Generate and play
        sam_->Say(audio_out_, upper);
    }
    
    void end() {
        delete sam_;
        delete audio_out_;
    }
    
private:
    SAM* sam_;
    AudioOutputI2S* audio_out_;
};
\```

**Alternative: Talkie (LPC-10)**
\```cpp
#include <Talkie.h>

// Pre-encode common phrases
const uint8_t sorry_data[] PROGMEM = { ... };  // LPC-10 encoded

Talkie voice;
voice.say(sorry_data);
\```

## 6. API Design

### 6.1 FastAPI Endpoints

\```python
# Badge -> Backend

POST /api/stash/upload
    Body: multipart/form-data {audio: file, embedding: json, badge_id: str}
    Response: {"status": "queued", "job_id": "abc123"}

GET /api/stash/{job_id}/status
    Response: {"status": "completed", "transcription": "...", "corrected_label": 3}

# Backend -> Badge

GET /api/models/{model_type}/version
    Response: {"version": "1.0.1", "size": 6234567, "checksum": "md5hash"}

GET /api/models/{model_type}/download
    Response: Binary file stream

GET /api/embeddings/dataset
    Response: {
        "version": "1.0.0",
        "embeddings": [[...256 floats...], ...],
        "labels": ["query0", "query1", ...]
    }

POST /api/embeddings/add
    Body: {"embedding": [...], "label": 3}
    Response: {"status": "added", "dataset_version": "1.0.1"}
\```

### 6.2 Stashed Data Upload Format

\```
POST /api/stash/upload
Content-Type: multipart/form-data

--boundary
Content-Disposition: form-data; name="badge_id"

badge_001
--boundary
Content-Disposition: form-data; name="timestamp"

2024-11-28T14:30:52Z
--boundary
Content-Disposition: form-data; name="embedding"; filename="embedding.json"
Content-Type: application/json

{"embedding": [0.123, -0.456, ...], "dimension": 256, "score": 0.45}
--boundary
Content-Disposition: form-data; name="audio"; filename="recording.wav"
Content-Type: audio/wav

<binary WAV data>
--boundary--
\```

### 6.3 Transcription Webhook Flow

\```
1. Badge uploads stashed recording
   POST /api/stash/upload -> job_id

2. Redis queue receives job
   LPUSH transcription_queue {job_id, badge_id, audio_path, embedding}

3. Worker processes queue
   - Load audio from storage
   - Run Whisper transcription
   - Auto-classify if confidence > 0.8
   - Otherwise: mark for manual review

4. Correction UI (human in loop)
   - Display audio player + waveform
   - Show transcription + predicted label
   - Human selects correct label
   - Submit correction

5. Update embedding dataset
   - Add corrected embedding to dataset
   - Increment dataset version

6. Badge syncs on next WiFi connection
   GET /api/embeddings/dataset?since_version=1.0.0
   - Download incremental updates
   - Merge with local dataset
\```

## 7. Dataset Creation Pipeline

Based on `audio_semantic_xtts_ipynb`, create training dataset:

### 7.1 Colab Notebook Workflow

\```python
# Step 1: Define queries (10 semantic intents)
QUERIES = [
    "Show me the schedule",
    "Find a booth",
    "Navigate to room",
    "Add a contact",
    "Take a note",
    "View the map",
    "Check messages",
    "See my profile",
    "Join a session",
    "Connect with someone"
]

# Step 2: Generate synthetic variations with XTTS
from TTS.api import TTS
tts = TTS(model_name="tts_models/multilingual/multi-dataset/xtts_v2")

for query_idx, query in enumerate(QUERIES):
    for speaker_idx, speaker_wav in enumerate(SPEAKER_REFERENCES):
        variations = generate_text_variations(query, n=5)
        for var_idx, variation in enumerate(variations):
            output_path = f"dataset/{query_idx}/{speaker_idx}_{var_idx}.wav"
            tts.tts_to_file(
                text=variation,
                speaker_wav=speaker_wav,
                language="en",
                file_path=output_path
            )

# Step 3: Extract YAMNet embeddings for all samples
# Step 4: Train projection layer (1024->256)
# Step 5: Compute query centroids
# Step 6: Export for ESP32
\```

### 7.2 Projection Matrix Training

\```python
import tensorflow as tf
import numpy as np

# Load YAMNet embeddings (1024-dim)
X_train = np.load("yamnet_embeddings.npy")  # [N, 1024]
y_train = np.load("labels.npy")             # [N] (0-9)

# Simple linear projection
projection_layer = tf.keras.layers.Dense(256, use_bias=False)

# Triplet loss for learning similarity-preserving projection
model = tf.keras.Sequential([
    tf.keras.layers.Input(shape=(1024,)),
    projection_layer
])

# Train with contrastive loss
model.compile(optimizer='adam', loss='mse')
model.fit(X_train, X_train, epochs=100)  # Autoencoder-style

# Extract weights
projection_matrix = projection_layer.get_weights()[0]  # [1024, 256]
projection_matrix = projection_matrix.T  # [256, 1024] for efficient matmul

# Save for ESP32
projection_matrix.astype(np.float32).tofile("projection.bin")
\```

### 7.3 Query Embeddings Computation

\```python
# Compute centroid embedding for each query
query_embeddings = []
for query_idx in range(10):
    # Get all embeddings for this query
    mask = (y_train == query_idx)
    query_samples = X_projected[mask]  # [K, 256]
    
    # Compute centroid
    centroid = query_samples.mean(axis=0)
    centroid = centroid / np.linalg.norm(centroid)  # Normalize
    
    query_embeddings.append(centroid)

query_embeddings = np.array(query_embeddings)  # [10, 256]

# Save for ESP32
np.savez("embeddings/query_embeddings.npz",
         embeddings=query_embeddings,
         labels=QUERIES)

# Binary format for direct loading
query_embeddings.astype(np.float32).tofile("embeddings/query_embeddings.bin")
\```

## 8. Risk Mitigation

| Risk | Mitigation |
|------|------------|
| Memory fragmentation | Use single memory pool with reset between states |
| YAMNet too large | Use YAMNet-Lite (167KB) or distilled model |
| TTS quality poor | Pre-record common phrases as WAV fallback |
| Deep sleep current high | Verify LCD power-off, I2S driver shutdown |
| WiFi connection unreliable | Local-first design, queue stash uploads |
| Embedding similarity poor | Start with 50+ real voice samples, iterate |

# OAISYS25 Badge - Unified Firmware Implementation Plan

## Overview

Integrate 5 working prototypes into a single ESP32-S3 badge firmware with:
- Animated logo display with gyro rotation
- Deep sleep with shake-to-wake
- Wake word OR button activation
- Audio → embedding → similarity matching → LLM response pipeline
- Robotic TTS output
- Cloud model updates via FastAPI backend

---

## Part 1: ESP32 Firmware

### 1.1 State Machine Architecture

\```
                    ┌─────────────────┐
                    │      BOOT       │
                    └────────┬────────┘
                             │
                    ┌────────▼────────┐
        ┌──────────►│   LOGO_LOOP     │◄──────────┐
        │           │  (wake word ON) │           │
        │           └────────┬────────┘           │
        │                    │                    │
        │         5min idle  │  button/wake word  │
        │                    │                    │
        │           ┌────────▼────────┐           │
        │           │   DEEP_SLEEP    │           │
        │           │  (accel wake)   │           │
        │           └────────┬────────┘           │
        │                    │ shake              │
        │                    └────────────────────┘
        │
        │  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────┐
        │  │         INTERACTION FLOW                    │
        │  └─────────────────────────────────────────────┘
        │                    │
        │           ┌────────▼────────┐
        │           │   RECORDING     │ 3-5 seconds
        │           │ (unload wake)   │

        │                    │

### 1.3 Memory Management Strategy

**Problem**: PSRAM is ~8MB, but models compete for space:
- Wake word: ~700KB
- YAMNet + projection: ~1MB
- LLM: ~6MB
- Video buffer: ~2MB

**Solution**: Sequential model loading with explicit unload

\```cpp
// Memory pool reserved in PSRAM
#define ML_POOL_SIZE (6 * 1024 * 1024)  // 6MB for largest model
static uint8_t* ml_pool = nullptr;

// Each ML module uses pool, not direct ps_malloc
class MLModule {
public:
    virtual bool load(uint8_t* pool, size_t pool_size) = 0;
    virtual void unload() = 0;
    virtual size_t requiredMemory() = 0;
};

// State transitions trigger load/unload:
// LOGO_LOOP: wake_word.load()
// RECORDING: wake_word.unload()
// EMBEDDING: yamnet.load() → yamnet.unload()
// LLM_INFER: llm.load() → llm.unload()
// Return to LOGO_LOOP: wake_word.load()
\```

### 1.4 Module Interfaces

Each module follows `begin()`/`end()` pattern:

\```cpp
// video_player.h
class VideoPlayer {
public:
    bool begin(const char* mjpeg_path);  // Load video to PSRAM
    void play();                          // Decode one frame
    void pause();
    void resume();
    void setRotation(uint8_t r);
    void showText(const char* text);     // Overlay text, pause video
    void hideText();                      // Resume video
    void end();
};

// wake_word.h
class WakeWordDetector {
public:
    bool begin(uint8_t* pool, const char* model_path, const char* config_path);
    bool detect();       // Returns true on wake word
    void end();          // Free all memory
};

// yamnet_embed.h
class YamnetEmbedder {
public:
    bool begin(uint8_t* pool, const char* model_path, const char* proj_path);
    bool extract(int16_t* audio, size_t samples, float* embedding_out);
    void end();
};

// llm_core.h (already exists, minor adaptations)
class LLMInference {
public:
    bool begin(uint8_t* pool, const char* model_path, const char* tok_path);
    void generate(const char* prompt, void (*on_token)(const char*));
    void end();
};

// robot_tts.h
class RobotTTS {
public:
    bool begin();
    void speak(const char* text);  // Blocking, outputs to I2S speaker
    void end();
};
\```

### 1.5 Implementation Phases

#### Phase 1: Core Integration (Video + Button + State Machine)
**Goal**: Logo loops, button triggers state change, text overlay works

Files to create/modify:
- `oaisys_badge.ino` - Main state machine skeleton
- `config.h` - All pin definitions
- `display/video_player.cpp` - Copy from `00_video_loop`, add `showText()`
- `display/text_overlay.cpp` - LVGL label overlay on GFX canvas

Key tasks:
1. Copy `MjpegClass.h` and video player logic
2. Add LVGL initialization (from factory demo BSP)
3. Implement text overlay using `lv_label` on transparent layer
4. Wire OneButton for state transitions
5. Test: Logo plays, button shows "Hello World" text, button hides text

#### Phase 2: Wake Word + Recording
**Goal**: Wake word detection triggers recording mode

Files to create:
- `audio/mic_stream.cpp` - Continuous I2S mic input for wake word
- `ml/wake_word.cpp` - Adapted from `03_custom_wakeword`
- `audio/audio_recorder.cpp` - 3-5 sec recording to buffer

Key tasks:
1. Adapt wake word detector to use memory pool
2. Implement recording mode (stop wake word, record fixed duration)
3. Save audio to SD card in `/stash/` with timestamp
4. Test: Wake word triggers, records 5 sec, saves to SD

#### Phase 3: Embedding + Similarity Search
**Goal**: Extract embedding, find closest intent

Files to create:
- `ml/yamnet_embed.cpp` - Adapted from `04_yamnet_audio_embedding`
- `ml/embed_search.cpp` - Load embeddings.bin, cosine similarity

Key tasks:
1. Adapt YAMNet to use memory pool
2. Implement projection head (TFLite micro)
3. Load pre-computed embeddings from SD
4. Implement cosine similarity search
5. Test: Record → embed → find closest (print to Serial)

#### Phase 4: LLM Integration
**Goal**: High-confidence matches trigger LLM response

Files to modify:
- `ml/llm_core.cpp` - Adapt to use memory pool
- `display/video_player.cpp` - Stream text to display

Key tasks:
1. Adapt LLM to pool-based allocation
2. Implement streaming callback for token display
3. Stop video, show text character-by-character
4. Test: Matched intent → LLM generates → displays on screen

#### Phase 5: Robotic TTS
**Goal**: Speak responses with 90s robot voice

Files to create:
- `tts/robot_tts.cpp` - SAM or Talkie-based synthesis

**Recommended approach**: **Talkie library** (Arduino LPC speech)
- Proven on ESP32
- Very robotic sound (1980s Speak & Spell)
- Tiny memory footprint (~10KB)
- Pre-encoded phonemes, fast synthesis

Alternative: **ESP32-SAM** (Software Automatic Mouth port)
- More natural but still robotic
- Text-to-phoneme built in
- Slightly larger (~50KB)

Key tasks:
1. Integrate Talkie or SAM library
2. Configure I2S output to MAX98357A
3. Implement `speak()` with text-to-phoneme conversion
4. Test: Text → robotic speech output

#### Phase 6: Deep Sleep + Shake Wake
**Goal**: 5min idle → deep sleep, accelerometer shake → wake

Files to create:
- `sensors/sleep_manager.cpp` - Sleep/wake logic

Key tasks:
1. Configure RTC timer for 5-minute idle detection
2. Configure QMI8658 interrupt for motion detection
3. Use ESP32 ULP or ext1 wake source
4. Save/restore state across sleep
5. Test: Idle → sleep → shake → wake → resume logo

#### Phase 7: WiFi + Model Updates
**Goal**: Check server for new models, download if available

Files to create:
- `network/wifi_manager.cpp` - Connect from SD config
- `network/model_updater.cpp` - HTTP GET model manifest
- `storage/sd_manager.cpp` - File operations abstraction

Key tasks:
1. Parse `config.json` for WiFi credentials and server URL
2. Implement background WiFi scan (every 30s when idle)
3. Check model manifest endpoint
4. Download new models to SD, swap on next boot
5. Test: WiFi connects, checks manifest, downloads test file

#### Phase 8: Stash Upload + Low-Confidence Handling
**Goal**: Unrecognized audio uploaded for cloud transcription

Files to create:
- `storage/stash_manager.cpp` - Queue unrecognized audio
- `network/data_uploader.cpp` - Upload when 10 files accumulated

Key tasks:
1. Save [audio.wav, embedding.bin, score, timestamp] to `/stash/`
2. Count stashed files, trigger upload at 10
3. Package as multipart POST to server
4. Delete local files after successful upload
5. Play "Sorry, couldn't understand" via TTS

## Part 2: Cloud Backend (FastAPI + Redis)

### 2.1 Architecture

\```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    Lightsail Instance                       │
│  ┌─────────────┐  ┌─────────────┐  ┌─────────────────────┐  │
│  │   FastAPI   │  │    Redis    │  │   File Storage     │  │
│  │   Server    │◄─┤    Queue    │  │   /data/models/    │  │
│  │   :8000     │  │   :6379     │  │   /data/stash/     │  │
│  └──────┬──────┘  └─────────────┘  │   /data/dataset/   │  │
│         │                          └─────────────────────┘  │
│         │                                                   │
│  ┌──────▼──────┐                                           │
│  │   Worker    │  Background transcription                  │
│  │  (rq/arq)   │  Whisper API or local                     │
│  └─────────────┘                                           │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
\```

### 2.2 API Endpoints

\```python
# Model Management
GET  /api/models/manifest
     Returns: {"wake_word": "v1.2", "yamnet": "v1.0", "llm": "v2.1", ...}

GET  /api/models/{model_name}
     Returns: Binary model file
     Headers: X-Model-Version: v1.2

POST /api/models/{model_name}
     Upload new model version (admin auth required)

# Stash Management
POST /api/stash/upload
     Multipart: audio files + metadata JSON
     Triggers: Background transcription job

GET  /api/stash/pending
     Returns: List of files awaiting correction

# Correction UI
GET  /api/corrections
     Returns: HTML page with audio player + text editor

POST /api/corrections/{id}
     Update transcription, add to training dataset

POST /api/retrain
     Trigger model retraining (admin auth required)

# Health
GET  /api/health
     Returns: {"status": "ok", "models_count": 5, "pending_transcriptions": 3}
\```

### 2.3 Data Flow

\```
ESP32 uploads stash (10 files)
        │
        ▼
POST /api/stash/upload
        │
        ▼
Save to /data/stash/{timestamp}/
Queue transcription job in Redis
        │
        ▼
Worker picks up job
Calls Whisper API (or local whisper.cpp)
Saves transcript to /data/stash/{id}/transcript.txt
Marks as "pending_review"
        │
        ▼
Admin opens /api/corrections
Listens to audio, edits transcript
Clicks "Save" → adds to /data/dataset/qa.csv
        │
        ▼
Admin clicks "Retrain"
Triggers training job (or manual Colab run)
New model uploaded via POST /api/models/llm
        │
        ▼
ESP32 checks GET /api/models/manifest
Sees new version, downloads model
Uses new model on next boot
\```

## Part 4: Key Implementation Details

### 4.1 Text Overlay on Video

Two approaches:

**Option A: LVGL Overlay (Recommended)**
\```cpp
// Initialize LVGL with transparent background
lv_obj_t* text_layer = lv_obj_create(lv_scr_act());
lv_obj_set_style_bg_opa(text_layer, LV_OPA_80, 0);  // Semi-transparent
lv_obj_set_style_bg_color(text_layer, lv_color_black(), 0);

lv_obj_t* label = lv_label_create(text_layer);
lv_label_set_long_mode(label, LV_LABEL_LONG_WRAP);
lv_obj_set_width(label, 220);

// Show text: pause video, show LVGL layer
void VideoPlayer::showText(const char* text) {
    paused = true;
    lv_label_set_text(label, text);
    lv_obj_clear_flag(text_layer, LV_OBJ_FLAG_HIDDEN);
}
\```

**Option B: Direct GFX Draw (Simpler)**
\```cpp
// After video frame decode, draw text on top
void VideoPlayer::showText(const char* text) {
    paused = true;
    gfx->fillRect(10, 200, 220, 100, BLACK);  // Text background
    gfx->setTextColor(GREEN);
    gfx->setTextSize(2);
    gfx->setCursor(15, 210);
    gfx->print(text);
}
\```

### 4.2 Wake Word → Recording Transition

\```cpp
void transitionToRecording() {
    // 1. Stop wake word detection
    wakeWord.end();  // Frees ~700KB PSRAM

    // 2. Reconfigure I2S for recording (same pins, different buffer size)
    recorder.begin(RECORD_DURATION_MS);

    // 3. Visual feedback
    video.showText("Listening...");

    // 4. Record
    int16_t* audio = recorder.record();  // Blocking, returns PSRAM buffer
    size_t samples = recorder.getSampleCount();

    // 5. Save to SD
    saveAudioToSD(audio, samples);

    // 6. Transition to embedding
    transitionToEmbedding(audio, samples);
}
\```

### 4.3 Cosine Similarity Search

\```cpp
// embed_search.cpp
class EmbeddingSearch {
    float* embeddings;      // 300 × 256 floats from SD
    char** intents;         // 300 strings from SD
    int count;

public:
    bool begin(const char* embed_path, const char* intent_path) {
        // Load embeddings.bin (307KB) to PSRAM
        embeddings = (float*)ps_malloc(300 * 256 * sizeof(float));
        File f = SD.open(embed_path);
        f.read((uint8_t*)embeddings, 300 * 256 * sizeof(float));

        // Load intents.txt (one per line)
        // ...
    }

    SearchResult search(float* query_embed) {
        float best_score = -1;
        int best_idx = -1;

        for (int i = 0; i < count; i++) {
            float score = cosineSimilarity(query_embed, &embeddings[i * 256], 256);
            if (score > best_score) {
                best_score = score;
                best_idx = i;
            }
        }

        return {intents[best_idx], best_score};
    }

private:
    float cosineSimilarity(float* a, float* b, int len) {
        float dot = 0, norm_a = 0, norm_b = 0;
        for (int i = 0; i < len; i++) {
            dot += a[i] * b[i];
            norm_a += a[i] * a[i];
            norm_b += b[i] * b[i];
        }
        return dot / (sqrtf(norm_a) * sqrtf(norm_b));
    }
};
\```

### 4.4 Robotic TTS with Talkie

\```cpp
// robot_tts.cpp
#include <Talkie.h>

// Pre-encoded vocabulary (LPC10 format)
// Generate using: https://github.com/going-digital/Talkie
extern const uint8_t sp_HELLO[];
extern const uint8_t sp_I[];
extern const uint8_t sp_AM[];
// ... more words

class RobotTTS {
    Talkie voice;

public:
    bool begin() {
        // Configure for I2S output instead of DAC
        voice.setPin(I2S_SPEAKER_DIN);  // May need custom Talkie fork
        return true;
    }

    void speak(const char* text) {
        // Simple word lookup (or use SAM for arbitrary text)
        // For MVP: pre-define common responses
        if (strstr(text, "sorry")) {
            voice.say(sp_I);
            voice.say(sp_AM);
            voice.say(sp_SORRY);
        }
        // ...
    }
};
\```

**Alternative: SAM (for arbitrary text)**
\```cpp
#include "SAM.h"

SAM sam;

void speak(const char* text) {
    sam.Say(text);  // Converts any text to speech
    // Output is 22kHz 8-bit, needs I2S adapter
}
\```

### 4.5 Deep Sleep with Accelerometer Wake

\```cpp
// sleep_manager.cpp
#include "esp_sleep.h"
#include "driver/rtc_io.h"

#define ACCEL_INT_PIN GPIO_NUM_XX  // QMI8658 INT pin (check schematic)

void enterDeepSleep() {
    // Save state to RTC memory
    RTC_DATA_ATTR static uint8_t last_rotation;
    last_rotation = video.getRotation();

    // Configure QMI8658 motion interrupt
    // (Set high-g threshold, enable interrupt output)
    configureAccelInterrupt();

    // Configure wake source
    esp_sleep_enable_ext0_wakeup(ACCEL_INT_PIN, 1);  // Wake on HIGH

    // Enter deep sleep
    esp_deep_sleep_start();
}

void setup() {
    if (esp_sleep_get_wakeup_cause() == ESP_SLEEP_WAKEUP_EXT0) {
        // Woke from shake - restore state
        video.setRotation(last_rotation);
    }
    // Normal boot...
}
\```

## Part 5: Testing Checkpoints

| Phase | Test | Pass Criteria |
|-------|------|---------------|
| 1 | Logo plays | MJPEG loops smoothly at 30+ FPS |
| 1 | Button pause | Single click pauses, click resumes |
| 1 | Text overlay | "Hello" appears over paused video |
| 1 | Gyro rotation | Tilting rotates display |
| 2 | Wake word | "Hey Daisy" triggers within 2 sec |
| 2 | Recording | 5 sec audio saved to SD as WAV |
| 3 | Embedding | YAMNet produces 256-dim vector |
| 3 | Similarity | Correct intent found for test phrase |
| 4 | LLM load | Model loads in <5 sec |
| 4 | Generation | Response streams to display |
| 5 | TTS output | Robotic speech audible from speaker |
| 6 | Deep sleep | Current drops to <10mA |
| 6 | Shake wake | Badge wakes and resumes logo |
| 7 | WiFi connect | Connects from SD config |
| 7 | Model check | Detects new version on server |
| 8 | Stash upload | 10 files uploaded successfully |
| Backend | Manifest | GET returns model versions |
| Backend | Transcribe | Uploaded audio gets transcript |
| Backend | Correction | UI allows editing and saving |

---

## Part 6: Risk Mitigation

| Risk | Mitigation |
|------|------------|
| PSRAM fragmentation | Use fixed memory pool, sequential load/unload |
| Wake word false positives | Tune threshold in config.json, add cooldown |
| Embedding mismatch | Start with high threshold (0.8), tune down |
| LLM hallucination | Train on exact Q&A, use low temperature |
| TTS unintelligible | Test Talkie vs SAM, choose clearer one |
| WiFi unreliable | Graceful degradation, work fully offline |
| Deep sleep instability | Test thoroughly, add watchdog timer |
| SD card corruption | Use safe write patterns, checksums |

---

   644→### 4.4 Robotic TTS with SAM (Software Automatic Mouth)
   645→
   646→**Chosen: SAM** - Any text input, classic 1980s computer voice
   647→
   648→SAM is the legendary Commodore 64 / Apple II speech synthesizer. It converts
   649→arbitrary English text to phonemes and synthesizes robotic speech. Perfect for
   650→that retro "talking computer" vibe!
   651→
   652→```cpp
   653→// robot_tts.cpp
   654→// Using ESP32-SAM port: https://github.com/pschatzmann/ESP32-SAM
   655→
   656→#include "ESP32SAM.h"
   657→#include "AudioOutputI2S.h"
   658→
   659→class RobotTTS {
   660→private:
   661→    AudioOutputI2S* out = nullptr;
   662→    ESP32SAM* sam = nullptr;
   663→
   664→public:
   665→    bool begin() {
   666→        // Configure I2S for MAX98357A speaker
   667→        out = new AudioOutputI2S();
   668→        out->SetPinout(6, 7, 8);  // BCLK, LRC, DOUT
   669→        out->SetGain(0.5);        // Volume control
   670→        out->begin();
   671→
   672→        sam = new ESP32SAM();
   673→        return true;
   674→    }
   675→
   676→    void speak(const char* text) {
   677→        // SAM handles text-to-phoneme conversion internally
   678→        // Output: 22050Hz mono audio
   679→        sam->Say(out, text);
   680→    }
   681→
   682→    // For more robotic effect, adjust voice parameters
   683→    void setRoboticVoice() {
   684→        sam->SetSpeed(72);      // Default 72, lower = slower
   685→        sam->SetPitch(64);      // Default 64, higher = squeakier
   686→        sam->SetThroat(128);    // Default 128, affects resonance
   687→        sam->SetMouth(128);     // Default 128, affects articulation
   688→    }
   689→
   690→    // Ultra robotic: pitch down, slow, mechanical
   691→    void setUltraRobotic() {
   692→        sam->SetSpeed(50);      // Slow and deliberate
   693→        sam->SetPitch(40);      // Deep, mechanical
   694→        sam->SetThroat(160);    // More robotic resonance
   695→        sam->SetMouth(100);     // Slightly muffled
   696→    }
   697→
   698→    void end() {
   699→        if (sam) { delete sam; sam = nullptr; }
   700→        if (out) { delete out; out = nullptr; }
   701→    }
   702→};
   703→
   704→// Usage in main sketch:
   705→RobotTTS tts;
   706→
   707→void setup() {

   709→    tts.setUltraRobotic();  // Maximum robot vibes!
   710→}

   714→    tts.speak(text);           // Speak robotically
   715→    delay(2000);               // Pause after speaking

   717→}

## Approved Plan:
# OAISYS25 Badge - Unified Firmware Implementation Plan

## Overview

Integrate 5 working prototypes into a single ESP32-S3 badge firmware with:
- Animated logo display with gyro rotation
- Deep sleep with shake-to-wake
- Wake word OR button activation
- Audio → embedding → similarity matching → LLM response pipeline
- Robotic TTS output
- Cloud model updates via FastAPI backend

---

## Part 1: ESP32 Firmware

### 1.1 State Machine Architecture

### 1.3 Memory Management Strategy

**Problem**: PSRAM is ~8MB, but models compete for space:
- Wake word: ~700KB
- YAMNet + projection: ~1MB
- LLM: ~6MB
- Video buffer: ~2MB

**Solution**: Sequential model loading with explicit unload

```cpp
// Memory pool reserved in PSRAM
#define ML_POOL_SIZE (6 * 1024 * 1024)  // 6MB for largest model
static uint8_t* ml_pool = nullptr;

// Each ML module uses pool, not direct ps_malloc
class MLModule {
public:
    virtual bool load(uint8_t* pool, size_t pool_size) = 0;
    virtual void unload() = 0;
    virtual size_t requiredMemory() = 0;
};

// State transitions trigger load/unload:
// LOGO_LOOP: wake_word.load()
// RECORDING: wake_word.unload()
// EMBEDDING: yamnet.load() → yamnet.unload()
// LLM_INFER: llm.load() → llm.unload()
// Return to LOGO_LOOP: wake_word.load()
```

### 1.4 Module Interfaces

Each module follows `begin()`/`end()` pattern:

```cpp
// video_player.h
class VideoPlayer {
public:
    bool begin(const char* mjpeg_path);  // Load video to PSRAM
    void play();                          // Decode one frame
    void pause();
    void resume();
    void setRotation(uint8_t r);
    void showText(const char* text);     // Overlay text, pause video

};

public:

};

// yamnet_embed.h
class YamnetEmbedder {
public:

// llm_core.h (already exists, minor adaptations)
class LLMInference {

// robot_tts.h
```

#### Phase 4: LLM Integration

#### Phase 5: Robotic TTS
**Goal**: Speak responses with 90s robot voice

Files to create:

**Recommended approach**: **Talkie library** (Arduino LPC speech)

## Part 2: Cloud Backend (FastAPI + Redis)

### 2.1 Architecture

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    Lightsail Instance                       │
│  ┌─────────────┐  ┌─────────────┐  ┌─────────────────────┐  │
│  │   FastAPI   │  │    Redis    │  │   File Storage     │  │
│  │   Server    │◄─┤    Queue    │  │   /data/models/    │  │
│  │   :8000     │  │   :6379     │  │   /data/stash/     │  │
│  └──────┬──────┘  └─────────────┘  │   /data/dataset/   │  │
│         │                          └─────────────────────┘  │
│         │                                                   │
│  ┌──────▼──────┐                                           │
│  │   Worker    │  Background transcription                  │
│  │  (rq/arq)   │  Whisper API or local                     │
│  └─────────────┘                                           │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

### 2.2 API Endpoints

```python
# Model Management
GET  /api/models/manifest
     Returns: {"wake_word": "v1.2", "yamnet": "v1.0", "llm": "v2.1", ...}

GET  /api/models/{model_name}
     Returns: Binary model file
     Headers: X-Model-Version: v1.2

POST /api/models/{model_name}
     Upload new model version (admin auth required)

# Stash Management
POST /api/stash/upload
     Multipart: audio files + metadata JSON
     Triggers: Background transcription job

GET  /api/stash/pending
     Returns: List of files awaiting correction

# Correction UI
GET  /api/corrections
     Returns: HTML page with audio player + text editor

POST /api/corrections/{id}
     Update transcription, add to training dataset

POST /api/retrain
     Trigger model retraining (admin auth required)

# Health
GET  /api/health
     Returns: {"status": "ok", "models_count": 5, "pending_transcriptions": 3}
```

### 2.3 Data Flow

```
ESP32 uploads stash (10 files)
        │
        ▼
POST /api/stash/upload
        │
        ▼
Save to /data/stash/{timestamp}/
Queue transcription job in Redis
        │
        ▼
Worker picks up job
Calls Whisper API (or local whisper.cpp)
Saves transcript to /data/stash/{id}/transcript.txt
Marks as "pending_review"
        │
        ▼
Admin opens /api/corrections
Listens to audio, edits transcript
Clicks "Save" → adds to /data/dataset/qa.csv
        │
        ▼
Admin clicks "Retrain"
Triggers training job (or manual Colab run)
New model uploaded via POST /api/models/llm
        │
        ▼
ESP32 checks GET /api/models/manifest
Sees new version, downloads model
Uses new model on next boot
```
